articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्षको बहारः ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बाग्मती प्रदेशको राजधानी हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ लाई लक्षित गर्दै ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइन लागिएको पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अन्तर्गत सरसफाइ थालिएको हो ।

यो वर्ष बाग्मतीको प्रादेशिक राजधानीस्थित हेटौँडा उपमहानगरपालिकाले पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मनाउँदैछ । पर्यटन वर्षको कार्यक्रम अन्तर्गत सून्य फोहोर अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । यहि अभियान अन्तर्गत शनिवार हातमा कुचो र बोरा बोकेर जनप्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षाकर्मी, टोल विकास संस्थाका पदाधिकारी र स्थानीयवासी सडकमा निस्किए । हेटौँडाका सडकदेखि टोलसम्म सरसफाइ गर्दै उनीहरूले ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियान शुरु गरेका हुन् ।

फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई केवल सरसफाइ अभियानका रूपमा नभई पर्यटन, वातावरण संरक्षण र नागरिक संस्कृतिसँग जोडिएको दीर्घकालीन अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइने योजना उपमहानगरपालिकाको छ । उपमहानगरपालिकाले ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइने पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अघि सारिएको हो ।

मुख्य तथा सहायक सडक, सार्वजनिक स्थल र पर्यटकीय क्षेत्रको सरसफाइसँगै वृक्षारोपण र सौन्दर्यीकरणलाई पनि अभियानको प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ । टोल विकास संस्था नगर समन्वय समितिको संयोजनमा सुरु भएको अभियान नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोल विकास संस्थामा सुरु गरिएको छ । पर्यटन वर्षको अवसरमा सुरु गरिएको ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियानले नगरको स्वच्छता र सौन्दर्य कायम राख्दै हेटौँडालाई पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यका रूपमा चिनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको दाबी छ ।

पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मा हेटौँडामा आन्तरिक तथा बाह्य पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउने उपमहानगरपालिकाको लक्ष्य छ । पर्यटकलाई आकर्षित गर्न नयाँ गन्तव्यको प्रचारसँगै शहरको स्वच्छता, सौन्दर्य र व्यवस्थित वातावरणलाई पनि प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ ।

यही उद्देश्यले सुरु गरिएको यो अभियानलाई नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोलसम्म विस्तार गरिँदैछ । टोल–टोलमा सरसफाइ र फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउँदै हेटौँडालाई स्वच्छ, सुन्दर र पर्यटकमैत्री शहरका रूपमा विकास गर्ने र पर्यटन वर्षमा बढीभन्दा बढी पर्यटक भित्र्याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

articles.title: इन्सेन्टिभ वितरण नहुँदा सेवा ठप्प, मर्कामा सर्वसाधारण विरामी
articles.summary:
महोत्तरी । प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा सेवा लिन आउने नागरिक अनाहकमा पिडित बन्न पुगेका छन । मेडिकल सुपिरिटेंडेन्ट, अस्पताल संचालन तथा व्यस्थापन् समिति अध्यक्ष बिचको तालमेल समस्या र भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको बाकी इन्सेन्टिभ जस्ता आन्तरिक विवादका कारण सेवाग्राहीलाई मर्का परिरहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा अस्पतालमा भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा बन्द भएपछि बिरामीहरू निजी स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा महँगो शुल्क तिरेर सेवा लिन बाध्य छन् । अस्पताल प्रशासनले प्राविधिक कारणले सेवा वन्द रहेको सूचना टॉस गरि सेवा अवरुद्ध रहेको बताएको छ । तर भित्री कुरा भने भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने चिकित्सकलाई इन्सेन्टिभ उपलब्ध नगराइएका कारण सो सेवा विगत दुई हप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि वन्द रहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवले इन्सेन्टिभकै समस्याको कारणले दुईहप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा सुचारू हुन नसकेको स्विकारे । आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\०८३ मा चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएका कारण सेवा वन्द गरेको बताउदै समस्या समाधानको पहल गरिरहेको निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवको भनाइ छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका अस्पताल सञ्चालन तथा व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष रोहित प्रसाद ठाकुरले पनि काम गर्ने चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएकै कारणले सेवा अवरुद्ध भएको बताए । उनले सेवा सुचारुको पहल गरिरहेको बताउदै अस्पताल व्यवस्थापन समितिको जेठ २८ गते बसेको बैठकले इन्सेन्टिभ दिने निर्णय गरेपनि सो किन वितरण गरिएन ? आशंका छन् ।

स्वास्थ सेवा जस्तो संवेदनशील संस्थाले अस्पतालको आन्तरिक तथा प्रशासनिक समस्याकै कारण सेवा ठप्प पार्नु, आम नागरिकलाई अनाहकमा समस्या दिनु स्वभाविक रुपमा लिन सकिदैन्। तर, यसको समाधान कसरी होला? सर्वसाधारणले नै सोध्न थालेका छन् ।

articles.title: Check what’s on your plate: Growing sale of unhygienic food rings alarm bells
articles.summary:
Shashi Thapa has fallen sick from food poisoning twice in the past four months.

Thapa, a final-year management student who also works at a private logistics company, relies on eating out for breakfast and lunch and, on most days, dinner too.

“I ate fish and naan at a local eatery near my room for dinner. That night I couldn’t sleep because of loose motion and nausea,” said Thapa, who lives in a rented room. “I had a fever the next day.”

Thapa went to the hospital the following day, where a test confirmed food poisoning.

Government officials say there are no exact figures on the number of food contamination cases because such incidents can occur at schools, colleges, offices, hotels and restaurants, and even at airports.

But they say cases of food contamination are rising alarmingly across Nepal’s cities. Many people who move to cities for work or study—and even longtime residents—depend on eating out for most of their meals. Nearly all of them report at least one, if not repeated, bout of illness from contaminated food.

For instance, Anjita Rokaya, owner of Aashal Pharmacy in Tinkune, sees two to three people coming in daily with bowel and other health-related problems.

“The patients usually say that they eat something outside,” she said. “Most of the visitors are adults and children.”

Another pharmacy reported a similar pattern.

Ecolife Pharmacy in Tinkune says 15-20 people visit daily with gut-related problems.

Among them, 10-12 cases are related to food poisoning.

“We provide them with oral rehydration and medicine to control diarrhoea and vomiting, and recommend going to hospital if the medicine does not help,” said Pradip Joshi, owner of the pharmacy.

The most common symptoms of food poisoning are diarrhoea, stomach pain and cramps, nausea, vomiting and fever.

The sale of poor-quality and unhygienic food has been rampant—from hotels and restaurants and eateries to party palaces.

Government data too tell the story.

The Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection conducted inspections at 261 hotels and restaurants, mostly in Kathmandu, last fiscal year 2025-26, which ended in mid-July, and found 59 selling unhygienic food. These eateries were fined Rs4.2 million, but no cases were filed. This shows that more than two out of every 10 hotels and restaurants inspected were found selling substandard fare.

The remaining hotels and restaurants were instructed to maintain food safety and hygiene.

In 2024-25, the department inspected 201 hotels and restaurants, of which 44 were found selling unhygienic food.

Anil Kirati, director of the Commerce Department, said that, as per the law, the department slaps fines between Rs200,000 and Rs300,000 on the spot if eateries are found selling substandard food.

“We have received a flurry of complaints from consumers about unhygienic food at hotels and restaurants in the past few months.”

In April, the quality watchdog filed a case against the Tripureshwar-based Bagmati Sweets at the District Administration Office, Kathmandu, for serious violations of hygiene and quality standards.

Manufactured or packaged food have also been found to be unsafe.

In May, Nepal’s quality watchdog recalled a batch of Dabur Honey after laboratory tests found the product to be of low quality.

The Department of Food Technology and Quality Control recalled batch NB00477 of honey produced by Dabur Nepal.

According to the department’s laboratory test report, the Dabur honey was found to contain hydroxymethyl furfural (HMF) at 50 milligrams per kilogram, above the food standard of 40 milligrams per kilogram. A high level of HMF in honey indicates that the product has been overheated, stored improperly or is very old.

In the same month, the department recalled a batch of CO2 Nova ice cream produced by the Pokhara-based Fishtel Dairy.

A sample test conducted on Current and Lali brands of noodles produced by Yasoda Foods found the acid value of the extracted fat to be below the standard determined by the government.

Recently, the Jack Nack Krakers biscuit brand produced by Asian Biscuit and Confectionery, Duhabi, Sunsari, was also recalled from the market after its fatty acid value was found to exceed the government-prescribed standard. Biscuits from ‘batch 6’ were recalled from the market.

In February, the department recalled and destroyed Khajurico brand puff, a popular snack, after laboratory tests found industrial trans fat levels exceeding the permissible limit. Around 5,200 packets were pulled from the market and crushed and buried within the factory premises in Godavari, Lalitpur.

Every year, the department inspects restaurants, hotels, and manufactured and packaged food across the country. But improvements from these inspections are barely visible, even as cases continue to rise.

Government data show that inspections are increasing but are not keeping pace with the growing number of contamination cases.

In the last fiscal year, the department conducted 12,806 market inspections—on its own and jointly with other agencies—across the country. The inspections covered food and feed factories, hotels and restaurants, and highway eateries, largely in response to public complaints. That amounts to an average of 35 inspections a day, mostly concentrated in urban areas. The inspection count has grown from 11,059 in the previous fiscal year.

Officials say the nature of complaints, ranging from poor hygiene and labelling violations to outright contamination and adulteration, is worsening.

“We receive complaints through our official phone line, written letters and Hello Sarkar on a daily basis,” said Bal Kumari Sharma, spokesperson for the department, the quality watchdog.

“Most complaints involve foreign objects in food, including hair, metal, eggshells and plastic. Others mention spoiled ingredients.” Hello Sarkar is the government’s grievance-handling system that operates through phone, email and social media.

Last Monday, food safety officials in Gauridhara seized and destroyed three packets of momo and four packets of chowmein that did not have complete labels, along with two packets of artificial food colouring, at the Local Thakali Restaurant and Bar Pvt Ltd.

A day later, inspectors found a cockroach infestation in the kitchen of New Dudh Sagar restaurant at Machhapokhari, Balaju. Less than two weeks ago, Burger King and Crunchy Fried Chicken restaurant in Chandragiri was found storing food uncovered inside refrigerators, along with other hygiene lapses.

The World Health Organisation estimates that unsafe food causes around 866 million illnesses and 1.5 million deaths annually, many of which could be prevented through measures including improved water, sanitation and hygiene, food safety practices such as pasteurisation, and access to healthcare for vulnerable populations.

Exposure to biological hazards, including foodborne bacteria and viruses as well as parasitic infections, caused the majority of foodborne illnesses—approximately 860 million in 2021—while chemical exposures drove a disproportionate share of deaths.

Beyond health impacts, the study estimates that in 2021 foodborne disease led to about $310 billion in lost productivity, measured in time away from work due to illness. When the economic impact was adjusted for cost-of-living differences between countries, the estimate increased to $647 billion in lost productivity.

While these recent enforcement actions highlight the scale of the problem, Sharma, the department’s spokesperson, said the rise in complaints reflects both growing consumer awareness and continued negligence by food businesses.

Food contamination and adulteration are not new in Nepal, but a regulatory system that struggles to oversee a vast informal food economy has created a deep crisis of consumer trust.

Small eating outlets known as khaja ghar, which offer affordable meals, typically operate on thin margins and rarely meet even basic hygiene standards. Workers skip hygiene protocols and ingredients go unchecked.

Nepal does have rules meant to prevent this.

The Food Safety and Quality Control Act 2024 governs how food is made, stored, transported and sold. Under the law, food safety officers are responsible for inspections, sample collection and investigating complaints.

“The Food Safety and Quality Control Act has laid out standards for how food should and shouldn’t be handled. The implementing regulations are yet to come,” said Sharma, the department’s spokesperson.

In practice, consumers remain exposed to unsafe food on a routine basis.

Restaurant owners say most kitchens operating across the country lack basic infrastructure, including proper exhaust systems, fire extinguishers or proper drainage.

“Like with hotels, the government needs to set minimum standards for restaurants, categorise them, and divide inspection responsibility between local, provincial and central governments based on that categorisation,” said Sangharsha Bista, president of the Restaurant and Bar Association Nepal (Reban), the umbrella organisation of restaurants.

“Owners and staff also need training on maintaining hygiene.”

Bista said restaurants and local eateries are supposed to register with local governments, which are then responsible for inspections, but in practice, local-level inspections rarely happen.

Consumer rights activists say food is often tested only after complaints surface or suspicions are raised. But by that point, contaminated or adulterated food may already have been consumed or sold elsewhere.

Madhav Timilsina, president of the Consumer Rights Investigation Forum, said hotels and restaurants are covered by both the Consumer Protection Act and the Food Safety and Quality Control Act 2024. Even so, he said, violations remain widespread: adulterated food at party palaces and hotels, low-quality or cheap cooking oil, substandard meat and fish, and foreign objects turning up in food.

“Restaurant and eatery operators aren’t being held accountable because inspections are seasonal at best, and the Department of Food Technology can’t handle this alone,” Timilsina said. “With local governments failing to fulfil their duties, consumers are left eating contaminated food, and the state has failed to guarantee food safety.”

Public health experts warn that eating contaminated food carries both immediate and long-term health risks.

Sharad Raj Onta, a retired professor of Community Medicine and Public Health at the Institute of Medicine, said poor toilets and drinking-water management, workers not washing their hands or covering their hair, and improperly cleaned kitchen utensils all contribute to food contamination.

“Over the long term, contaminated food can cause hepatitis, jaundice and infections in different parts of the digestive system,” Onta said. Chemical contamination in food, he added, can also damage the kidneys, nervous system and blood.

In October 2017, Nepal’s Department of Food Technology issued a directive making it mandatory for hotels and restaurants to meet food quality, safety and hygiene standards. The directive, endorsed by the Ministry of Agriculture, classified eateries into four categories based on food quality, service and infrastructure: very good, good, medium and average.

Under the directive, hotels and restaurants are required to follow Good Manufacturing Practice, Good Hygiene Practice and Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point principles to protect consumer health.

But these principles are hardly practised.

“This is a serious matter,” Onta said. “We need a systematic and strict inspection process.”

articles.title: What happens when press freedom meets right to privacy
articles.summary:
The arrest of Kishor Shrestha, journalist and editor of Jana Aastha weekly, on Wednesday, has triggered a sharp debate, with opinions divided over two difficult but closely connected questions: the freedom to publish and the right to personal privacy.While one side, largely from the media fraternity, argues that criminal charges should not be brought over the subject matter of a news report, the other side, including media consumers and observers, has questioned the nature of the report itself.

Shrestha was taken into custody after a woman filed a complaint alleging an offence against personal privacy.

The arrest has its roots in a Jana Aastha report published on August 5 headlined “Honourable’s ‘Lip Kiss’ with Another Woman”. The report carried a photograph showing Amarkant Chaudhary, a member of the House of Representatives elected from Saptari Constituency-3 on behalf of the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), kissing a woman.

The report claimed that the woman who filed the complaint had shared the photograph on her Facebook wall, stating, “...the young woman has shared the photograph on her Facebook wall.”

The fact that Shrestha was arrested on the basis of the woman’s complaint is also mentioned in the detention warrant. The letter, signed by investigating officer Police Inspector Lok Krishna Dahal, states: “...on the complaint filed by [name omitted], in the case relating to an offence against personal privacy in which the Government of Nepal is the plaintiff and you are the defendant, it being necessary to keep you in police custody for investigation, you are hereby given this detention warrant and shall be kept in police custody from today’s date.”

The dispute the arrest has triggered, however, is not simply about whether the report was responsible journalism. It raises a broader question about the route the state should take when published material is alleged to violate privacy: when does such a complaint remain a matter of media regulation, and when can it become a matter for the criminal justice system?

The Federation of Nepali Journalists, the umbrella organisation of journalists in Nepal, has described the arrest as an attack on press freedom, basing its argument on Nepal’s existing laws, including the Journalists’ Code of Conduct, 2016, the Press Council Act, 1992, and the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, which guarantees press freedom.

The code of conduct provides guidance on what journalists should or should not publish. The Council Act, 1992 provides the Press Council Nepal with mechanisms to deal with violations of the code, including requiring media organisations to publish a response or correction, issue an apology or publish a comment from an aggrieved party. In cases of repeated violations, the council can recommend the withdrawal of government facilities or benefits and can publicly express its disapproval.

The federation argues that if published material was found to have breached an individual’s privacy, the aggrieved party should first have approached the Press Council Nepal, and that the police action was therefore unwarranted.

“The jurisdiction to deal with issues that are not satisfactory in a news report lies with the Press Council Nepal. The federation’s position is that using government machinery in this manner against journalist Shrestha, while misusing that jurisdiction, is against press and freedom of expression, the journalists’ code of conduct and the Constitution,” the umbrella body of Nepali journalists said in a statement.

But the legal framework does not necessarily require the council process to be exhausted before the criminal justice system can be invoked. The council’s role is primarily tied to violations of journalistic standards and the code of conduct. Where published material is alleged to constitute a criminal offence under a separate law, such as the Privacy Act, the matter can fall outside the council’s jurisdiction.

Umesh Shrestha, the council’s chair, said it can order a media organisation to publish its decision when it finds a violation of the code. He said that if such an order is repeatedly ignored, it can also recommend further action under existing provisions.

“For example, after repeated non-compliance, the council can recommend suspension of a press pass to the relevant authority,” Umesh told Kantipur. “But the council itself does not have the authority to suspend a press pass. That power rests with the Department of Information and Broadcasting.”

According to Umesh, the department has not implemented such recommendations, saying its own rules do not provide for suspension. “There is a legal obstacle in this,” he said. “The council’s role is therefore primarily tied to questions of journalistic conduct and professional responsibility.”

The debate also raises a broader question about how press freedom is understood in Nepal. While it is often invoked in terms of the freedom of journalists and media organisations to publish, observers say that freedom also carries questions of responsibility, including how the public can assess the information it receives and how media organisations are held accountable for what they publish.

National Women Commission chair Kamala Parajuli has also cautioned against using press freedom as a justification for violating privacy.

Speaking to Kantipur after raising the issue in a social media post, Parajuli said journalists should not treat press freedom as a licence to publish anything they want.

“Press freedom does not give anyone the right to attack or violate an individual’s privacy at will by taking shelter under the notion that journalists are not required to disclose their sources,” she said. “Women have only recently begun to enter public life in greater numbers. They should not be subjected to this kind of mental harassment, and the media and social media platforms need to take this issue seriously.”

Nepal’s legal framework therefore provides different routes for different kinds of complaints. A violation of the journalistic code can be taken to the council, while certain violations of privacy can trigger criminal investigation by the police. Other privacy-related claims can be pursued directly through the courts, while defamation has a separate legal route.

That distinction is important in Shrestha’s case. The central legal question is not simply whether the complainant should have approached the council first, but what exactly was alleged against Shrestha, under which provision of law, and whether that alleged conduct constitutes a criminal offence.

Nepal’s Privacy Act provides specific protections for personal privacy. It defines personal information to include, among other things, information relating to a person’s identity, address and contact details, documents, biometric information, criminal history and certain professional opinions.

The Act also protects a person’s private life. It prohibits making matters relating to a person public in a manner that affects the person’s private life, causes harm or brings the person into disrepute, subject to the exceptions and conditions set out in the law.

The Act provides criminal penalties for specified violations of its privacy provisions. Under Section 29(2), a person convicted of the relevant offence can face imprisonment of up to three years, a fine of up to Rs. 30,000, or both.

The police say Shrestha was arrested under this provision.

The detention warrant records the legal basis cited by police for taking Shrestha into custody. But it does not, by itself, answer a more fundamental question: what specific conduct in the published material is alleged to have constituted a criminal offence under the Privacy Act?

That question assumes importance because the report involved both a private individual and a sitting lawmaker. It also presented the photograph as something the woman herself had shared publicly on Facebook. Whether that fact has any bearing on the alleged privacy violation — and whether publication of material that has already been made public can itself constitute an offence — requires examination of the specific provisions of the Act and the circumstances in which the material was originally shared.

That is where the competing principles become harder to reconcile. A free press does not give journalists an unrestricted licence to publish private information. At the same time, the existence of privacy protections does not mean that every publication concerning a person’s private life is beyond legitimate journalism. The distinction depends on what was published, why it was published, whose privacy was affected, whether there was a legitimate public interest and what the law permits.

According to Tribhuvan University assistant professor Shree Ram Paudel, the freedom to publish and the right to privacy are subjects that invariably come up for debate. He argues that both public figures and journalists must be responsible in their respective roles.

“The fact that there is a right to privacy does not mean that nothing can be written at all,” Paudel told Kantipur. “But while exercising press freedom, journalists should not violate someone’s personal privacy and cross into the realm of a criminal offence.”

According to him, the conduct of public office holders such as ministers or MPs should also be dignified. If their activities fall within the public sphere, they must be responsible for their conduct.

“‘I have privacy’ cannot be a reason for them to escape becoming the subject of press coverage. But journalism should not seize only one side of an incident and engage in ‘clickbait’ or ‘news-selling’ journalism — journalism that is cheap and designed to sell,” assistant professor Paudel said. “When reporting news, the press must be conscious and responsible so that sensitive groups requiring protection, such as women, children or minorities, are not harmed.”

Santosh Sigdel, a lawyer and executive director of Digital Rights Nepal, argues that journalists’ conduct also comes into the discussion alongside journalistic freedom and privacy.

“One important aspect in determining whether a news report has violated privacy is whether the subject is a matter of public importance or public interest,” Sigdel said.

According to Sigdel, the character of an elected representative can become a matter of public interest and therefore can be a subject of news.

“But, in doing so, journalists must not forget the legal provisions protecting an individual’s privacy or the code of conduct, and must maintain a balance between the two,” he said.

The circumstances of the police action raise a further question. Police also searched the Jana Aastha office the following morning and seized computers and a mobile phone. The legal basis for that search and seizure, and whether police obtained the necessary authorisation, therefore become relevant to assessing the state’s response to the publication.

While Shrestha’s journalism is not free of controversy, his paper has in the past been credited with scoops. Yet Jana Aastha has also often been criticised for prying into people’s private lives and for publishing sensational material. Every time Shrestha, also a former chairperson of the council, lands in controversy, a 23-year-old news report resurfaces. Actor Shreeha Karki died by suicide after Jana Aastha published nude photographs of her, an incident that observers and journalists have cited as an example of journalism crossing ethical boundaries.

Lately, some of Jana Aastha’s reporting has been critical of the current administration, and those opposing Shrestha’s arrest have questioned whether the state machinery may have been mobilised against the journalist for that reason. The federation has described the arrest as part of a broader attempt to intimidate the media.

The arrest has put some in the media fraternity in a difficult position. While supporting the freedom to publish, some have also stressed journalistic accountability, arguing that no one, including journalists, is above the law. Their concern, however, is that legitimate accountability mechanisms should not be used to target journalists or restrict legitimate journalism, and that due process is followed when such mechanisms are invoked, including in Shrestha’s case.

Journalists speaking privately also pointed to a responsibility that extends beyond the formal code of conduct: individual journalists and media organisations must define their own standards for deciding what should and should not be published. For them, self-regulation remains an essential part of a healthy media environment.

Umesh, the council’s chair, said the council draws a distinction between a violation of journalistic ethics and a violation of criminal law.

“A complaint over a publication alleged to have violated privacy could fall within the council’s jurisdiction to the extent that it raises questions about compliance with the journalists’ code of conduct,” Umesh told Kantipur. “The code requires journalists to respect personal and professional privacy except where doing so would adversely affect the public interest.”

He acknowledged that the question of journalistic ethics and the question of a legal offence can arise separately from the same incident.

“Which process applies depends on the nature of the alleged conduct, the applicable law and the relevant legal procedure,” Umesh said. “While the council examines the ethical dimension within its jurisdiction, determining criminal liability or other legal liability rests with the competent legal authorities or courts.”

For the Nepali media, the issue now goes beyond the Shrestha arrest, leaving it with a difficult question: how can journalistic freedom and the right to privacy be protected at the same time, without either becoming a shield against accountability?

articles.title: Lawmaker’s verbal clash with police chief raises questions over parliamentary conduct
articles.summary:
Jaya Singh Mahara

Kathmandu, August 14

A heated exchange between ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Khagendra Sunar and Nepal police chief Dan Bahadur Karki at a parliamentary committee meeting has sparked a wider debate over Nepal’s parliamentary decorum.

Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal and RSP chair Rabi Lamichhane have taken an interest in the exchange, which occurred during Wednesday’s meeting of the Public Accounts Committee. Aryal has summoned Karki for a meeting on Friday to discuss the incident and the conduct expected of lawmakers and officials appearing before parliamentary committees.

RSP whip Prakash Chandra Pariyar confirmed that Aryal would meet Karki on Friday.

“The inspector general of police will meet the speaker on Friday,” Pariyar said. “They will discuss what happened at the parliamentary committee meeting and the issue of parliamentary decorum.”

Aryal had already sought an explanation from the Public Accounts Committee leadership on Thursday. He summoned the committee chair, Bharat Bahadur Khadka, and the secretary, Babita Mishra, to ask what had transpired during the exchange between Sunar and Karki.

Khadka said the speaker wanted to understand what had happened after the heated exchange received widespread media coverage.

“I told him that I had already facilitated the proceedings and explained what happened at the meeting,” Khadka said.

According to Khadka, he also told the speaker that lawmakers, including those from the ruling RSP, should not demoralise or make personal allegations against the country’s security chiefs.

Aryal stressed that lawmakers should use respectful language when raising issues in parliamentary committees and observe the dignity of their office. He also said lawmakers and invited officials should be mindful of their respective positions and the sensitivity of issues under discussion.

Lamichhane has separately sought details of the dispute. He summoned Pariyar on Thursday and asked what had happened at the committee and how the matter could be resolved.

“The chair was concerned because the issue had appeared in the media,” Pariyar said. “He said discussions should be conducted in a dignified manner.”

The clash occurred during a committee discussion on a complaint alleging irregularities in the purchase of uniforms for election police. Home secretary Raj Kumar Shrestha, Karki and Armed Police Force chief Narayan Dutta Poudyal had been summoned to respond to the allegations.

During Wednesday’s meeting, Sunar made strong accusations over the uniform procurement and called for the Public Accounts Committee to form a probe panel. He also demanded that the home secretary and the police chiefs resign or be suspended while the investigation was conducted.

“We should investigate it. The discussion will be bitter,” Sunar said. “Serious issues must be discussed in the committee. I stand with the soldiers and the lower classes.”

He then called for former home minister Om Prakash Aryal, the home secretary and the inspector general of police to be suspended and removed from their responsibilities pending an investigation.

“If you have a conscience, you should resign,” Sunar said. “If this is a state governed by law, you should be dismissed. This must happen today, right now.”

Karki objected to what he described as comments that could damage the integrity of police personnel and the reputation of the institution.

“People who have worked with integrity until today are brought here and told whatever people feel like saying,” Karki said. “This is not a place where you can say whatever you want. There must be some basic standard of decorum anywhere.”

Karki also appeared to suggest that he could bring complaints against lawmakers before the committee in response.

Shrestha said he was willing to have his personal and family assets investigated and that he had nothing to fear from a probe. Poudyal likewise said the Armed Police Force would cooperate with any investigation.

Sunar left the committee meeting before it ended, saying other lawmakers had been too accommodating towards the invited government officials and police chiefs.

He has since continued to target Karki on social media.

On Thursday, Sunar wrote on Facebook that someone had to take the risk of confronting those in power, whatever the cost. He said the dispute over the police uniforms could not be settled simply by officials invoking their uniforms and ranks.

Sunar said he stood with police personnel and temporary election police who, he said, came largely from poor families. He accused officials of being involved in a serious corruption case involving billions of rupees spent on shoes, socks, underwear and food rations for low-ranking personnel.

“Someone accused in a case should give a statement, not a sermon,” Sunar wrote. On Wednesday, Sunar had also posted a message aimed at Karki, rewriting lyrics from a song Karki had written.

“Mother, I rose from the ashes,” Sunar wrote, twisting the original lyrics to accuse Karki of looting a country that had been reduced to ashes and escaping after allegedly manipulating the system when corruption allegations were made.

articles.title: Man-made water hazards are becoming a deadly monsoon trap for children
articles.summary:
The monsoon brings the familiar threat of floods and inundation to Nepal’s southern plains. But for children, another danger is often closer to home: water collecting in pits, construction sites, open drains and unfinished infrastructure.

Roadside excavations, holes dug for brick kilns, ponds, irrigation canals and trenches around culverts and bridges can become deadly traps once filled with rainwater. The danger is often invisible. Children may have no way of judging how deep the water is before stepping in to play, bathe or swim.

Last Friday, 7-year-old Khushi Alam drowned in a water-filled pit beside a culvert in ward 5 of Yamunamai Rural Municipality, Rautahat district.

Khushi had gone to play with four or five friends at a culvert about a kilometre west of his home. His friends returned in the evening, but Khushi did not. When he failed to come home late into the night, relatives and neighbours began searching for him. His father reported him missing at a police post in Bamanhar.

Police eventually found Khushi’s body in a pit about 20 feet south of the culvert along the Satbamba road.

Ward chair Shivendra Sah said the pit had existed for years and had filled with rainwater.

“It is an old pit beside the road,” Sah said. “It is difficult to fill it, and it cannot simply be left as it is. Children are attracted to such water-filled pits, but the consequences are becoming serious.”

The ward has since conducted awareness programmes at schools and urged children to stay away from stagnant water.

Khushi’s death was far from an isolated case in Rautahat or the wider Madhesh province.

On July 28, two sisters, 5-year-old Puchki and 3-year-old Ghaghari, drowned in a water-filled excavation near an under-construction bridge in Chakradaha, in ward 26 of Birgunj Metropolitan City, Parsa district.

The girls, daughters of Prabhu Thakur of Sughauli, had gone to a field with their grandfather, Kishori Thakur. The family arrived at about 11am. Their grandfather left the children briefly while he went to call their grandmother. When he returned, the girls were gone.

Their family searched nearby and contacted relatives. Their mother, Antima Devi, reported them missing to the Sughauli Area Police Office that night. Police found both girls dead the following morning in the flooded pit near the bridge.

In Siraha district, three children from the same family died in another water-filled excavation on July 12.

The children, 12-year-old Sabnam Khatun, 10-year-old Rubina Khatun and 7-year-old Saiful Sheikh, drowned while bathing in a pit at a livestock market in Choharwa, ward 7 of Golbazar Municipality. Residents and security personnel pulled them from the water and took them to the hospital, where doctors pronounced all three dead.

Golbazar Mayor Shyam Kumar Shrestha said the pit had been there for years and was used as a water source for livestock.

“We never imagined such an incident could happen,” Shrestha said. “We will fence the area rather than fill the pit, as it is used like a pond for animals.”

He said the municipality would also run awareness campaigns.

In Mahottari district, three girls drowned on May 22 in the village of Sarpallo in ward 7 of Manarashiswa Municipality. The victims were 12-year-old Sneha Kumari and 6-year-old Shivani Kumari, daughters of Birendra Bhandari, and 12-year-old Afsana Khatun, daughter of Aziz Nadaf.

Police said the girls had gone swimming at the confluence of the Ankushi and Jangha rivers. They slipped while bathing and were swept into deeper water.

That same day, 2-year-old Deepika Kumari, daughter of Naresh Mahato, drowned in rainwater that had collected in a field near her home in Rajkhor village, ward 4 of Gaushala Municipality.

Mahottari Assistant Chief District Officer Sanjay Kumar Pokharel blamed a lack of public awareness for the recurring deaths.

“We repeatedly tell local governments at every disaster-management meeting to fill dangerous pits,” Pokharel said. “We even make policy decisions on the issue. But it is unclear whether elected representatives are ignoring them or what is happening.”

The incidents show that children are not drowning only in rivers, streams and natural water bodies. Water collecting in roadside pits, culverts, construction sites, farmland and old excavations around settlements can be just as deadly.

A recurring seasonal tragedy

The scale of drowning deaths among children in Madhesh is stark.

According to the Madhesh Province Police Office in Janakpur, 608 children have drowned in the province’s eight districts over the past seven fiscal years, from 2019-20.

Rautahat recorded the highest number, with 110 child deaths. Dhanusha reported 102, Siraha 81, Saptari 75, Mahottari 71, Bara 66, Sarlahi 60 and Parsa 43.

Police data show that many of the deaths do not occur in major rivers or natural lakes. Children are frequently killed in culverts, irrigation channels, deep pits excavated for brickmaking, ponds and roadside trenches.

The pattern points to a problem that extends beyond parental supervision.

Former Madhesh provincial assembly member Dhan Lal Thokar said poorly managed infrastructure and unsafe excavation were major contributors.

“Brick kilns, soil excavation sites and roadside culverts are routinely left open after construction,” Thokar said. “Villages often lack safe places for children to play, so they end up around water-filled pits and culverts. This is not simply an unfortunate accident or a failure of parental care.”

The problem is particularly acute around brick kilns, where deep pits are dug to extract soil and can later fill with rainwater.

Rautahat Chief District Officer Dinesh Sagar Bhusal said local units had repeatedly been asked to fill dangerous pits or secure them with fences and warning signs.

“We have told elected representatives again and again,” Bhusal said. “We are tired of repeating ourselves. Yet they simply do not act. It is becoming a serious problem.”

He said brick kiln operators often excavate soil deeper than permitted and leave the pits exposed.

“Such pits are much deeper than ordinary ponds and are therefore particularly dangerous for children,” Bhusal said. “Contractors working on roads, bridges and culverts also leave excavations open, either during construction or after the work is completed. Soil is removed during road widening, but the pits are not filled or secured.”

The risk is compounded by poverty.

Police investigations indicate that many children who drown in pits, culverts, brick kiln sites and ponds come from poor or low-income households. Parents who have to work long hours to support their families may be unable to supervise young children closely, leaving them free to wander into ponds, canals and construction sites.

Madhesh Finance Minister Yuvaraj Bhattarai said child safety should be treated as a responsibility shared by families, communities and the state.

“Pits dug in the name of development must no longer take the lives of innocent children,” he said. “The Madhesh government is serious about this.”

On July 5, the secretariat of Janamat Party chair CK Raut said more than 450 children had drowned in ponds and pits in Madhesh over the previous four years. The party argued that the deaths should not be treated simply as natural disasters because many could have been prevented.

It called for open pits in villages and neighbourhoods to be filled or fenced, warning signs and barriers to be installed around ponds, brick kilns and construction sites, and greater supervision of young children around water. It also urged schools and communities to conduct water-safety programmes and local governments to identify and regularly monitor dangerous sites.

The same danger in Lumbini

The problem extends beyond Madhesh.

In the western province of Lumbini, ponds, rivers, irrigation canals and reservoirs are important sources of water, but they also pose a growing drowning risk, particularly during the hot months and monsoon.

In Dang district, an average of about one person dies each month from drowning or being swept away by water, according to Superintendent of Police Dipak Shrestha, chief of District police in Dang. Last fiscal year, 29 people died in such incidents.

Some deaths occur when people who cannot swim enter the water carelessly. Others happen during floods or accidents. Victims have drowned in natural rivers and lakes as well as artificial reservoirs built for irrigation or recreation.

In November 2024, three 12-year-old girls drowned while bathing in the Rapti river.

In June 2024, floodwaters in the Rapti river swept away 62-year-old Maniram Chaudhary of Lamahi Municipality. Seventeen-year-old Raj Kumar Yadav of Rajpur Rural Municipality also drowned while returning home after selling milk. Two teenagers died after being swept away by the Babai river in June.

The broader provincial figures show how widespread the risk is. Lumbini recorded 553 disaster incidents in the past four months, killing 90 people. Sixty of those deaths were caused by drowning, and four people remain missing. Twenty-three of the drowning victims were children.

Last fiscal year, the province recorded 1,837 disasters that killed 297 people. Drowning accounted for 190 deaths, with 14 people still missing.

In Rupandehi district alone, two children and one woman drowned within three months, according to the Butwal Area Police Office. On July 11, 15-year-old Pragya Gautam of Tilottama drowned in a fishpond. She went into the water at about 6pm and was not pulled out until around 9pm.

On May 17, 18-year-old Umakanta Chaudhary of Butwal drowned while swimming in the Tinau River.

Police Inspector Thamman GC said drowning incidents increase during periods of extreme heat, when children and teenagers go swimming in rivers, canals and ponds.

“Children, particularly those aged 11 or 12 and above, often go swimming in groups to escape the heat,” GC said. “They may not know how deep the water is, and that can lead to drowning.”

He said victims were often from low-income or working-class families, or households where parents were away at work.

Last fiscal year, 17 people drowned in Rupandehi, including nine men and eight children. Seven of the children were boys, and one was a girl.

Lumbini authorities have called for stronger safety measures around water infrastructure.

Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya, who also chairs the provincial disaster management council, said the government was stepping up awareness campaigns during the monsoon.

“Fencing irrigation canals, ponds and other dangerous water bodies and putting warning signs around public ponds and dams can reduce the risk,” Acharya said. “Local governments have also been instructed to conduct awareness campaigns around canals, ponds, irrigation channels and rivers and to discourage children from swimming in them.”

Prevention remains the missing link

Despite repeated warnings, dangerous sites remain scattered around settlements.

The problem is not limited to natural hazards. In many cases, the danger is created by development itself.

A contractor digs a trench for a culvert and leaves it open. A brick kiln extracts soil and abandons a deep pit. A road project removes earth without restoring the site. A pond or canal is left without a fence or warning sign. Rain then fills the excavation, turning it into a hidden hazard.

“The common factor in Madhesh and Lumbini is the failure to identify water and excavation hazards in places children can reach,” said Dang police chief Shrestha. “In some places, construction pits are left open. In others, there are deep excavations made for brick kilns. Elsewhere, canals, ponds and rivers have no warning signs. Sometimes parental supervision is weak. In other cases, local units and construction companies have failed to do their part.”

Madhav Narayan Municipality Mayor Baijnath Yadav said local units, landowners, industrialists and brick kiln operators all have a role in preventing deaths. Deep excavations should be fenced and marked with warning signs, while old pits that cannot be filled should at least be secured.

Every ward, he said, should map dangerous sites and arrange immediate safety measures. Municipalities should also create safe spaces where children can play instead of turning to construction sites and water-filled pits.

Yadav said his municipality plans to expand public awareness campaigns and provide training on emergency rescue and first aid for drowning victims.

Civil society leader Kedar Thapa of Rautahat said children’s safety must be built into development projects from the beginning.

“Development should improve people’s lives, not become a trap that takes their lives,” he said. “If the authorities do not act in time, more children will continue to disappear into water-filled pits.”

articles.title: Make inclusion a reality, not rhetoric
articles.summary:
When the Rastriya Swatantra Party came to power in March with a near two-thirds majority, Nepal, for the first time, saw roughly 35 percent women in the House of Representatives. Following this, Prime Minister Balendra Shah appointed six women ministers to his 17-member Cabinet. Even as ministers from the Khas-Arya dominate the ministry leadership, those from the Madheshi, Janajati and Dalit communities are also represented. For a country that has long struggled to place women in top leadership positions, the government’s move was historic and commendable. It also instilled hope that it would prioritise inclusivity in all vital appointments.

But beyond the Cabinet, the government’s appointments to constitutional bodies, commissions, universities and cultural institutions are far from inclusive. Between March 27 and August 11, the Cabinet made more than 50 appointments, of which only four were women. Madheshis, Janajatis and Dalits were thinly represented; Muslims were entirely excluded. Similarly, there isn’t a single woman among the three appointments to the Election Commission; nor are there any people from the Madheshi community. This is a continuation of the disregard of inclusion by previous governments. Even in senior university appointments, the notion of inclusion has been flouted: The government recently appointed seven university vice-chancellors, but not a single woman made the list. Appointments to state-run cultural academies failed to reflect the country’s regional gap and ethnic diversity.

The government justifies the appointments as being based on merit and open competition. It is true that Nepal’s public institutions are in dire need of competent people and should be free from political patronage, but the Balendra Shah government must internalise the idea that excluding people from marginalised communities from vital positions entails exclusion of an array of diverse views, inviting criticisms that the state still views them as ‘incompetent’. These institutions cannot be run by a cluster of historically privileged groups, with a similar worldview.

The Constitution recognises inclusion as the fundamental principle of the state. Hence, it is also vital to ask: What does merit mean in a country where access to education, job opportunities and institutions has often sidelined women, Janajatis, Madheshis and Dalits? Centuries-old social hierarchies, such as the caste system, regional disparities and gender discrimination have resulted in structural inequality in Nepal. Underrepresented groups cannot remain marginalised because they lack sufficient representatives to work for their upliftment and representation. Nepal cannot afford to push them back further.

The current Cabinet is considered the youngest and most academically qualified in the country’s history. They have repeatedly promised not to repeat the political practices of old parties. Being transparent about recent appointments would be a good start, but that is not enough. What’s more vital is for them to understand that they should prioritise inclusion in key appointments not only to correct historical exclusion faced by marginalised communities and people from remote regions but also to ensure that those positions aren’t reserved for the privileged few. If they don’t correct their course, they will lose the confidence of the marginalised communities who also voted them to power. They must break the cycle of exclusion, just as they did in Parliament and the Cabinet.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s new political darling is losing its spark
articles.summary:
For quite a long time, Nepalis had no option but to vote in conformity with their old political fan clubs, merely serving their own interests rather than the greater good. They never fostered bigger dreams. After long-serving, tested politicians failed to perform better, ‘change’ became a buzzword throughout the nation. Fueled by public anger and frustration, some urban and suburban Nepalis formed an ideologically unanchored party in 2022 and called it Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), which translates to National Independent Party—practically implying freedom from any old political doctrines.

The new party mesmerised the public with hype and charm, deploying a set of fresh faces in national media after a long time. The RSP brand quickly became the talk of the town, especially in the middle-class segments of rural and urban Nepal.

As a reaction to aggressive gerontocracy in almost all institutional domains and particularly to the social media ban imposed by the UML government, Nepal witnessed a Gen Z revolt on September 8-9, 2025. The uprising resulted in the bloodshed of 76 Nepalis all over the country, with an estimated Rs85 billion worth of loss. The aftermath of the Gen Z movement further exacerbated the need for urgent change in mainstream politics, threatening the shares of political power of the old parties—the Nepali Congress, the UML and the Maoists (now NCP). This led to a call for a snap election in the country, putting the RSP brand in an advantageous position.

The RSP alone was unable to encash this situation as they were not fully able to imbibe the spirit of the Gen Z movement owing to their fragile ideological and methodological standing. So, a significant space was provided to the urban elites who somehow managed to show their faces and create viral, decent political reels during the movement.

Enter the viral part-time rapper, full-time Mayor of Nepal’s biggest metropolis Balendra Shah in the RSP show.

Shah, hailing from the Madheshi community and with approximately 58 percent of the total national votes coming from Madhesh province, was a sound marketing strategy for RSP’s PM candidacy. His candidacy also stood for political revenge against prevailing gerontocracy dominance. The new ‘Balen’ flagship featured in the RSP brand sent ripples in the public sphere.
