articles.title: Book review: What Binod Chaudhary’s memoir says about making it in Nepal
articles.summary:
The country’s sole dollar billionaire, Binod Chaudhary’s, new memoir, ‘Made in Nepal: Lessons in Business Building from the Land of Everest’, is, above all, a window into his mind. The truthfulness with which Chaudhary writes is striking. He does not attempt to conceal facts that may portray him in a bad light. He is, for example, upfront about the relationship between business and politics.

“Businessmen politicians were a reviled lot,” he says in the part talking about his political journey. He has written with a type of awareness that most of the rich and powerful lack.

At the beginning of his work is a note addressing protests last September, in which he points to Nepal’s staggering economic inequality as the issue at the core of what motivated protestors. This is a welcome understanding for the man, alongside being a lawmaker and, one would imagine, an influential donor, but the understanding does not seem to translate for him into support for left-wing policy. It comes across as more a distrust of Nepal’s politicians and bureaucrats than an aversion to policies aimed at helping the poor itself.

“Nobody can make Binod Chaudhary a communist,” he says in a part where he talks about almost getting a ticket from the CPN-UML. The same party, however, he shares, dropped a policy proposing higher taxes on Nepal’s hyperwealthy, in part because of his lobbying, so I suppose the ‘communist’ in CPN-UML is as little an indication of ideology as his membership in the party is.

The book follows Chaudhary’s journey as he takes over his father’s business and takes it to the heights he did. It was a journey full of many mistakes and betrayals. Chaudhary comes across as both shrewd and naive at the same time. On the one hand, over and over again, he is taken advantage of by lying, scheming, and swindling business partners, and on the other hand, he seems to manage to react in time and well enough to come out on top.

While reading the book, one comes across a long sentence, about four lines long. The following four lines repeat the same sentence in full, almost verbatim, with only a few words replaced. There are many other errors throughout my editions of the book, suggesting that whoever was responsible for finalising the manuscript did a rather slack job.

Some stories Chaudhary shares feel like straight fiction, like things that could never happen in real life, yet have happened to him and those around him. A standout example is when a sitting minister forces Chaudhary’s sons to donate a large sum of money to the PM fund during the Covid-19 pandemic, money that CG had otherwise raised for its own aid efforts.

On that note, the book tells readers a great deal about CG’s philanthropic efforts in Nepal. Of the many projects that the billionaire had overseen, the most impressive are his works in the aftermath of the 2015 Gorkha earthquake and during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Chaudhary is not shy, except in a handful of cases, about naming people with whom he has clashed in the past and detailing how they tried to wrong or harm him. I suppose the point of a business book is to teach readers business lessons; the book’s name would also suggest the same. The biggest lesson in the book is not about business management or efficiency creation, but that people can be really nasty and conniving with each other.

The author is guilty of assuming the best of people; he pays for this mistake at times. It makes him alert but does not tip him over the edge into someone weary of their colleagues.

‘Made in Nepal’ is a good reminder of who gets to become rich in a country like Nepal. And the answer is often those with ancestral wealth and connections with the ruling class.

Prince Dhirendra saves Binod Chaudhary from ruin in the book. This is not my takeaway; the author says as much. Saved from whom, you ask? A leader from the RPP, whose opponent Chaudhary had backed during a bid for power.

In a country like Nepal, power gives just as easily as it threatens to take away. To get to where CG is, one needs Binod Chaudhary’s discipline and brilliance, but one also needs a few generations’ worth of connections and rapport with strong families with deep roots. As long as that does not change, social inequality will remain, and so will the people’s discontent with it.

Made In Nepal: Lessons in Business Building from the Land of Everest

Author: Binod Chaudhary

Publisher: Harper Business

articles.title: Can meditation help people living with dementia?
articles.summary:
Last Spring, I was in Sydney, Australia, working on my research project and carrying my dream of permanently residing in the country. After decades of professional research and engagement, I was preparing for my new life abroad.

One day, I received a message that suddenly changed my life. I learned that one of the most loving members of my family had been diagnosed with dementia.

As I began researching the disease, I found that, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), dementia is the seventh leading cause of death globally. In 2021, around 57 million people worldwide were living with dementia. The WHO also reports that more than 10 million new cases are recorded each year. In 2019, dementia was linked to around 1.6 million deaths worldwide.

It was surprising to learn that around 60 percent of people living with dementia are in developing and least-developed countries, where healthcare facilities are often limited. The disease also places an enormous burden on individuals, families, and national economies.

According to the report, the global economic burden of dementia is around $1.3 trillion a year, including direct medical expenses and care costs. Without greater investment in early diagnosis, prevention, timely treatment, caregiver support and public health services, the WHO estimates that the economic burden of dementia could rise to $2.8 trillion by 2030.

This news was devastating for me, as it is for many families facing similar situations around the world. Dementia is not merely a disease that causes memory loss; it can also affect a person’s emotions, communication skills, and personality, while placing a profound emotional and financial burden on the entire family.

The diagnosis brought fear, uncertainty, and many unanswered questions. At that point, my dream of settling in Australia became less important. My priority was to return to my homeland and ensure that my loved one received the care and treatment they needed.

I immediately returned to Nepal and began making inquiries about healthcare services. Like many others I encountered during my research, I wanted to understand the condition better and find the best possible treatment for my loved one.

The search for medical treatment

My first step was to consult a psychiatrist. After evaluating the condition of the patient, the psychiatrist prescribed two tablets to be consumed every evening for 21 days.

We carefully followed the medical advice. However, within the first week of treatment, my loved one developed severe anxiety. The emotional distress increased, and I became concerned about whether the medication was producing the desired effect.

After completing the prescribed courses, I decided to seek another opinion. A second psychiatrist reviewed the condition and added another medication for one month. The psychiatrist also suggested that, after completing the treatment, brain imaging focusing on the hippocampus should be conducted.

The hippocampus is one of the brain’s most important structures for learning and memory. Pioneering researchers Dr Heiko Braak and Dr Eva Braak, neuropathologists at the University of Ulm in Germany, found that changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease often begin in specific brain regions involved in memory before spreading to other areas of the brain.

Unfortunately, after the additional medication, my loved one became physically weaker. Watching someone so precious lose strength was heartbreaking.

Concerned about this deterioration, I consulted another psychiatrist who was also the professor and mentor of the previous psychiatrists. After reviewing the complete medical history and treatment response, he adjusted the medical plan.

Gradually, the condition became more stable. Anxiety reduced, physical strength improved, and daily activities became easier.

This experience taught me an important lesson: dementia care requires patience, continuous observation, and individualised treatment. Every person responds differently, and medical decisions should be carefully monitored.

Introducing meditation as complementary care

Although medical treatment helped stabilise the condition, I realised that dementia care involves much more than medication. Dementia affects emotional health, confidence, sleep, and personal connection with the surrounding world.

Having practiced meditation for three decades and trained as a mindfulness meditation teacher, I decided to introduce gentle meditation sessions into my loved one’s daily routine.

The sessions were simple and adapted according to ability. They included mindful breathing, relaxation practices, loving-kindness meditation, and moments of peaceful awareness.

Initially, maintaining attention was difficult. However, with patience and regular practice, meditation gradually became a comforting part of daily life.

Over time, I observed encouraging changes. My loved one became calmer than before, anxiety reduced, sleep improved, and emotional stability increased. Meditation did not bring back the lost memories or cure dementia, but it appeared to create greater peace, comfort, and emotional balance. This personal experience encouraged me to explore the scientific evidence behind meditation and dementia care.

What science says about meditation and the brain

Modern neuroscience has increasingly examined how meditation influences the brain, emotions, and stress responses.

One of the most influential studies was conducted by Dr Madhav Goyal and colleagues at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine in the USA. Their Systematic review and meta-analysis, published in JAMA Internal Medicine in 2014, analyzed clinical trials involving thousands of participants. The researchers found that mindfulness meditation programs were associated with improvements in anxiety, depression, and psychological stress.

Dr Goyal and his colleagues emphasized that mediation must not replace medical treatment but can serve as a valuable complementary approach for improving mental well-being.

For people living with dementia, emotional symptoms such as anxiety, agitation, depression, and sleep difficulties can significantly reduce the quality of life. Therefore, approaches that improve emotional regulation may have meaningful benefits.

Meditation, neuroplasticity and the brain health

One of the most fascinating discoveries in neuroscience is neuroplasticity—the brain's ability to adapt and reorganise throughout life.

Research by Dr Sara W Lazar, an Associate Professor of Psychology at Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital, USA, provided important evidence on meditation and brain structure. Using MRI technology, Dr Lazar and her team found that experienced meditators showed differences in cortical thickness in brain regions associated with attention, sensory processing, and emotional regulation.

Their findings suggested that meditation experience may be associated with changes in brain areas involved in cognitive and emotional functions.

Further research by Dr Yi-Yan Tang, Distinguished Professor at Texas Tech University, USA, Dr Britta K Holzel of the Technical University of Munich, Germany, and Dr Michel I Ponser of the University of Oregon, USA, examined the neuroscience of mindfulness meditation. Their reviews explained that mindfulness practices influence the brain networks involved in attention, self-awareness, emotional regulation, and stress management.

These findings are important because dementia involves changes in many of these same brain systems. However, researchers caution that meditation cannot reverse dementia related brain damage. Instead, it may help strengthen emotional resilience and improve quality of life.

Meditation, stress and dementia caregivers

Dementia affects not only the person diagnosed but also the caregivers. Family members often experience emotional exhaustion, stress, anxiety, and uncertainty.

Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), developed by Dr Jon Kabat-Zinn at the University of Massachusetts Medical School, USA, has become one of the most widely studied mindfulness programmes in the world. His research demonstrated that mindfulness practices can help people manage stress, pain, and emotional challenges.

Researchers involving dementia caregivers have also shown encouraging results. Dr Kirk Warren Brown, Professor of Psychology at Virginia Commonwealth University, USA, and his colleagues studied mindfulness-based approaches for caregivers of people with dementia. Their findings suggested improvements in stress management, emotional resilience, and psychological well-being.

A healthier caregiver can create a more supportive and compassionate environment for the person living with dementia.

Meditation is not a cure, but it can support healing

It is important to maintain scientific honesty. Meditation is not a cure for dementia. Current evidence does not show that meditation can stop Alzheimer’s disease, restore damaged brain cells, or replace medical treatment. However, meditation is a safe, affordable, and non-invasive practice that may complement conventional care. When combined with appropriate medication, physical activity, cognitive stimulation, healthy nutrition, and meaningful social relationships, meditation may contribute to improved emotional health and quality of life.

The goal of dementia care should not only be to add years to life but also to add life to those years.

A journey that changed my purpose

My journey from Sydney back to Kathmandu transformed my understanding of life. I lost one dream, but I discovered another purpose: to serve the needy, like my loved one.

Caring for my dearest loved one taught me that healing is now always about eliminating disease. Sometimes healing means reducing fear, creating a moment of peace, preserving dignity, and offering unconditional presence. Every meditation session reminds me that love, compassion, and patience are powerful forms of care. Dementia may affect memory, but it cannot erase the human need for connection and affection.

The future of dementia care should embrace an integrated approach combining modern medicine with scientifically supported practices such as meditation, mindfulness, exercise, healthy lifestyle choices, and compassionate caregiving.

Sometimes the greatest healing does not come only from medicine; it rather comes from being fully present with someone we love.

articles.title: इरानको हारपछि हर्मुज अमेरिकाको हुनेछ : ट्रम्प
articles.summary:
अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले इरानलाई पराजित गरेपछि हर्मुजको जलमार्गलाई अमेरिकी क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्ने बताएका छन्।

उनले शुक्रबार न्यूयोर्कमा आफ्ना समर्थकहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उक्त टिप्पणी गरेका हुन्। उनी न्यूयोर्कमा रिपब्लिकन पार्टीको र्‍यालीलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै थिए।

ट्रम्पको यो बयान अमेरिका र इरानले लगभग छ महिना लामो द्वन्द्व अन्त्य गर्न सम्झौतामा पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेका बेला आएको हो। उनको बयानपछि इरानले पनि बदला लियो।

उपविदेशमन्त्री काजेम घरिबाबादीले हर्मुज इरानको भूभाग सधैँ रहिरहने बताए। यसलाई ट्वीट वा चुनावी भाषण मार्फत खोस्न नसकिने उनले बताए। उनले भने, 'इरान न त धम्कीबाट डराउँछ न त कुनै शक्तिको अगाडि झुक्छ।'

हर्मुज जलमार्गलाई विश्वको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण समुद्री मार्गहरू मध्ये एक मानिन्छ। यसले धेरै देशहरूमा तेल, प्राकृतिक ग्यास र मल ढुवानी गर्दछ। युद्ध सुरु हुनुभन्दा पहिले विश्वको तेल आपूर्तिको लगभग २० प्रतिशत यसबाट गुज्रन्थ्यो।

ट्रम्पले इरानलाई 'दुष्टताले भरिएको देश' भनेर वर्णन गरे र भने कि जबसम्म द्वन्द्व जारी रहन्छ तबसम्म अमेरिकीहरू पेट्रोलको उच्च मूल्यको लागि तयार हुनुपर्छ। उनले भने, 'यदि इरानलाई आणविक हतियार विकास गर्नबाट रोक्ने हो भने, अमेरिकीहरूले पेट्रोलको लागि अलि बढी तिर्न तयार हुनुपर्छ।'

articles.title: मोदीको ८०औँ स्वतन्त्रता दिवस सम्बोधन : एआईदेखि आत्मनिर्भर भारतसम्म, यी हुन् महत्त्वपूर्ण घोषणा
articles.summary:
भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले ८०औँ स्वतन्त्रता दिवसका अवसरमा लाल किल्लाबाट राष्ट्रलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै एक करोड युवालाई एआई तालिम दिने घोषणा गरेका छन्।

सो अवसरमा उनले नक्सलवाद, आत्मनिर्भर भारत, ऊर्जा र २०४७ सम्म विकसित भारत बनाउनेलगायत लक्ष्यबारे पनि जोड दिएर बताए। मोदीले भारतले पछिल्ला वर्षमा विभिन्न क्षेत्रमा गरेको प्रगतिको चर्चा गर्दै अब देश साना सपनामा सीमित भएर बस्न नहुने बताए। उनले ठुला सपना र बलियो संकल्पबाट मात्रै भारतलाई नयाँ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउन सकिने सुनाए।

उनले नक्सलवादको विषयमा बोल्दै सशस्त्र नक्सलवाद कमजोर भए पनि त्यसको विचारधारा फरक रूपमा सक्रिय हुन सक्ने चेतावनी दिए। उनले भने, ‘हामीले नक्सलवाद अन्त्य गर्ने संकल्प गरेका थियौँ। धेरै क्षेत्र नक्सलमुक्त भएका छन्। सशस्त्र नक्सल गए, तर मानसिक नक्सलहरू अवसर खोजिरहेका छन्।’ उनका अनुसार यस्ता समूहले समाजलाई गलत बाटोमा लैजान सक्छन्। त्यसैले त्यस्ता गतिविधि र विचारलाई समयमै पहिचान गर्नुपर्ने आजको आवश्यकता हो।

मोदीले स्वतन्त्रता दिवसको अवसरमा युवाका लागि ठुलो घोषणा गर्दै आगामी एक वर्षमा भारतका एक करोड युवालाई आर्टिफिसियल इन्टेलिजेन्स (एआई) सम्बन्धी तालिम दिने बताए। उनले प्रविधि र नवप्रवर्तनलाई भारतको विकासको महत्त्वपूर्ण आधारका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेका हुन्। मोदीले थप भने, ‘अब समय डेटा सेन्टर र एआईको हो। हामी भारतलाई नवप्रवर्तनको केन्द्र बनाउन चाहन्छौँ। त्यसैले एक करोड युवालाई एआईको तालिम दिइनेछ।’

मोदीले भारत स्वतन्त्र भएको १०० वर्ष पूरा हुने सन् २०४७ सम्म देशलाई विकसित राष्ट्र बनाउने लक्ष्य दोहोर्‍याए। उनले भने, ‘आज भारतले ठुलो सपना देखेको छ। त्यो सपना हो, २०४७ मा स्वतन्त्रताको १०० वर्ष पुग्दा विकसित भारत बनाउने।’ यो लक्ष्य पूरा गर्न देशका नागरिकको सामूहिक प्रयास आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ थियो। उनले विगतमा दशकौँ लाग्ने काम अब केही वर्षमै पूरा गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनले भारतको कार्यशैली र सोचमा पनि परिवर्तन आवश्यक रहेको कुरामा जोड दिए। उनका अनुसार विकासको गति बढाउन पुरानो सोच र काम गर्ने शैलीबाट बाहिर निस्कनुपर्छ। मोदीले भारतले अन्य देशमा अत्यधिक निर्भर भएर बस्न नहुने बताए। उनले आत्मनिर्भरतालाई देशको दीर्घकालीन हितसँग जोडेर व्याख्या गरेका हुन्। चीनतर्फ लक्षित गर्दै मोदीले भने, ‘भारत अब अरू देशमा निर्भर भएर बस्नु हुँदैन। हामी आत्मनिर्भर बन्नुपर्छ। संसारमा धेरै कुरा सस्तो र छिटो पाइन्छ, तर त्यसले हाम्रो आफ्नै क्षमता निर्माण गर्दैन। त्यसैले हामीले आफ्नो क्षमता बढाउनुपर्छ।’

मोदीले राजनीतिक स्थिरता, संविधान, न्याय व्यवस्था र उत्पादन क्षमताका कारण विश्वले भारतको क्षमता पहिचान गर्न थालेको दाबी गरे। उनले दाबी गर्दै भने, ‘आज भारतमा राजनीतिक जनादेश छ, देशमा स्थिर सरकार छ, संविधान छ र बलियो न्याय व्यवस्था छ। त्यसैले अब विश्वले हाम्रो क्षमतालाई चिन्न थालेको छ।’ भारतीय औषधि, कपडा, मेसिनलगायत उत्पादन विश्वका विभिन्न बजारमा पुगिरहेको उनको भनाइ छ।

ऊर्जा सुरक्षाको चर्चा गर्दै मोदीले पाइपमार्फत ग्यास आपूर्ति विस्तार भएको बताए। उनका अनुसार २०१४ अघि भारतका करिब ७० सहरमा मात्रै पाइपबाट ग्यास आपूर्ति हुने व्यवस्था थियो। अहिले यो सङ्ख्या ७०० सहरसम्म पुगेको छ। मोदीले अनुसार २०१४ अघि करिब २० देखि २२ लाख घरमा पाइपबाट ग्यास पुग्ने गरेकोमा अहिले एक करोड ७५ लाख घरमा यस्तो सुविधा पुगेको सुनाए।

उनले सौर्य ऊर्जाको उत्पादन क्षमता बढेको पनि बताए। उनका अनुसार भारतको सौर्य ऊर्जा क्षमता अहिले १६० गिगावाट पुगेको छ। मोदीले ‘प्रधानमन्त्री सूर्य घर’ योजनाबाट लाखौँ घरमा सौर्य ऊर्जाको प्रयोग बढेको र केही घरको विद्युत् बिल शून्यसम्म पुगेको बताए। केही घरले अतिरिक्त विद्युत् बिक्री गरेर आम्दानीसमेत गर्न थालेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनका अनुसार संकल्प बलियो भए कठिन परिस्थिति र विपत्तिबाट बाहिर निस्कने क्षमता पनि बढ्छ। कोरोना महामारी र रुस तथा युक्रेन युद्धका क्रममा देखिएका चुनौतीको चर्चा गर्दै उनले कठिन परिस्थितिबाट भारत अगाडि बढिरहेको दाबी गरेका हुन्। एजेन्सी

articles.title: ला लिगाको नयाँ सिजन आजदेखि, पहिलो दिनमै दुई खेल
articles.summary:
स्पेनिस फुटबलको सबैभन्दा ठूलो घरेलु प्रतियोगिता ला लिगाको २०२६-२७ सिजन आजदेखि सुरु हुँदैछ। नयाँ सिजनको पहिलो दिनमै दुई खेल हुनेछन्।

सिजनको उद्घाटन खेलमा अलाभेस र गेटाफे आमनेसामने हुँदैछन्। घरेलु मैदानको फाइदा उठाउँदै अलाभेस जितसहित नयाँ अभियान सुरु गर्न चाहन्छ। यता गेटाफे पनि सुरुवाती खेलमै महत्वपूर्ण तीन अंक हात पार्ने योजनामा मैदान उत्रनेछ।

आजै हुने अर्को खेलमा सेभिया र रायो भालेकानो भिड्नेछन्। घरेलु मैदानमा सेभियामाथि जितको दबाब हुनेछ भने रायो पनि बलियो सुरुवात गर्दै अंक बटुल्ने लक्ष्यमा हुनेछ।

नयाँ सिजन सुरु भएसँगै सबैभन्दा ठूलो चर्चा भने बार्सिलोना र रियल मड्रिडको उपाधि भिडन्तलाई लिएर छ। पछिल्लो सिजनको प्रतिस्पर्धापछि यी दुई ठूला टोली फेरि उपाधिका लागि आमनेसामने हुनेछन्।

articles.title: पर्यटकीय स्थलमा विद्युत् सुविधा विस्तार
articles.summary:
अन्नपूर्ण गाउँपालिका-८ स्थित पर्यटकीयस्थल आलडाँडामा केन्द्रीय प्रसारण लाइनको सुविधा विस्तार भएको छ।

नेपाल विद्युत् प्राधिकरणले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘उज्यालो म्याग्दी’ कार्यक्रमअन्तरगत राम्चेदेखि आलडाँडासम्म प्रसारण लाइन विस्तार भएको हो।

नेपाल विद्युत् प्राधिकरण म्याग्दी वितरण केन्द्रका प्रमुख सत्यनारायण गामीका अनुसार बिजुली नपुगेका मोहरेडाँडा, फूलबारी, डाँडाखर्क र कालीबराहमा शीघ्र विद्युत् विस्तार हुनेछ। मोहरेडाँडा, फूलबारी, डाँडाखर्क, कालीबराह र अन्नपूर्ण-धौलागिरि पर्यटकीय गन्तव्य हुन्।

articles.title: इरानको हारपछि हर्मुज अमेरिकाको हुनेछ : ट्रम्प
articles.summary:
अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले इरानलाई पराजित गरेपछि हर्मुजको जलमार्गलाई अमेरिकी क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्ने बताएका छन्।

उनले शुक्रबार न्यूयोर्कमा आफ्ना समर्थकहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उक्त टिप्पणी गरेका हुन्। उनी न्यूयोर्कमा रिपब्लिकन पार्टीको र्‍यालीलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै थिए।

ट्रम्पको यो बयान अमेरिका र इरानले लगभग छ महिना लामो द्वन्द्व अन्त्य गर्न सम्झौतामा पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेका बेला आएको हो। उनको बयानपछि इरानले पनि बदला लियो।

उपविदेशमन्त्री काजेम घरिबाबादीले हर्मुज इरानको भूभाग सधैँ रहिरहने बताए। यसलाई ट्वीट वा चुनावी भाषण मार्फत खोस्न नसकिने उनले बताए। उनले भने, 'इरान न त धम्कीबाट डराउँछ न त कुनै शक्तिको अगाडि झुक्छ।'

हर्मुज जलमार्गलाई विश्वको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण समुद्री मार्गहरू मध्ये एक मानिन्छ। यसले धेरै देशहरूमा तेल, प्राकृतिक ग्यास र मल ढुवानी गर्दछ। युद्ध सुरु हुनुभन्दा पहिले विश्वको तेल आपूर्तिको लगभग २० प्रतिशत यसबाट गुज्रन्थ्यो।

ट्रम्पले इरानलाई 'दुष्टताले भरिएको देश' भनेर वर्णन गरे र भने कि जबसम्म द्वन्द्व जारी रहन्छ तबसम्म अमेरिकीहरू पेट्रोलको उच्च मूल्यको लागि तयार हुनुपर्छ। उनले भने, 'यदि इरानलाई आणविक हतियार विकास गर्नबाट रोक्ने हो भने, अमेरिकीहरूले पेट्रोलको लागि अलि बढी तिर्न तयार हुनुपर्छ।'

articles.title: Monsoon disasters leave 85 dead as rains continue
articles.summary:
At least 85 people have died in monsoon-related disasters across Nepal in four months, according to Nepal Police. The toll includes 19 deaths from floods, 35 from landslides, 26 from lightning strikes, four from heavy rain and one from an avalanche between April 14 and August 14.

The monsoon is still active, and the risk of floods, landslides and other weather-related disasters remains high.

Nine people have gone missing, 196 have been injured, and 1,735 families have been affected by monsoon-related disasters during the period, police said.

The toll is slightly lower than last year. Between April and August 2025, monsoon disasters killed 90 people, including 39 in floods, 20 in landslides, 30 in lightning strikes and one in heavy rain.

But persistent rain over the past four days has caused fresh deaths and widespread damage in several districts.

In Rolpa, four people were killed when a landslide buried a house in Sun Chhahari Rural Municipality-2 on Thursday night.

The landslide struck the Phalbang settlement of Gam at around 10pm. A team of police and residents recovered the bodies of 77-year-old Biru Gharti Magar, his 68-year-old wife Shani Gharti Magar and their 70-year-old neighbour Lali Gharti Magar at around 11:30am on Friday.

Police said Lali had been visiting the couple when the landslide buried their house.

In the same ward, 64-year-old Lami Gharti Magar was buried inside her house in Mangraru. Her body was recovered on Friday, according to Rolpa police chief DSP Panchakumar Bakhu.

On Wednesday, a landslide swept through the Kotalbara settlement in Thabang Rural Municipality-5, burying 13 people. The bodies of only 10 have been recovered so far.

In Bajura, a 20-year-old woman was killed after a landslide buried a house in Tamsu of Tribeni Municipality-9 on Thursday night.

Pratikshya Thapa was killed when a landslide triggered by continuous rain swept down from above the house and buried the homes of residents Dharma Thapa and Karna Bahadur Thapa. Dharma Thapa, 40, and Dhauli Rawal, 40, were injured and are receiving treatment at Bajura District Hospital, Chief District Officer Dorendra Niraula said.

Pratikshya’s parents are in India. Her body has been kept at the district hospital.

Authorities held discussions with local officials and the district disaster management committee on Friday over relocation and other measures as the rain continued and the risk of further landslides increased, Niraula said.

In neighbouring Jajarkot, floods washed away five houses in Roli of Nalgad Municipality-10.

The homes of Prithivi Bahadur BK, Khaite BK, Nar Bahadur BK and Hasta BK were swept away. A tin shed and snack shop operated by Suntali BK on land belonging to Bir Bahadur BK were also destroyed.

Thirty-eight people living in the houses and sheds were moved to safer locations.

The local administration and security agencies were assessing damage in other areas, officials said.

Police and Armed Police Force personnel were deployed from Dalli to rescue residents at risk and move them to safety.

Flooding has also completely blocked the Jajarkot-Dolpa section of the Bheri Corridor. Vehicles travelling to Dolpa and those heading towards Jajarkot have been stranded along the route, leaving passengers and freight carriers stuck midway and disrupting road links with Dolpa.

With floods, landslides and road blockages disrupting daily life, authorities have urged residents to remain alert as further damage is possible.

In Baglung, eight families have been displaced by a landslide in Nisikhola Rural Municipality-2.

The landslide struck the Dharatole settlement on Friday afternoon after rocks and debris came down from the Brengri-Handichaur road, damaging houses and cattle sheds.

The homes and sheds belonging to Dhan Bahadur Chhetri, Rajan Pariyar, Narayan Kunwar, Tara Gharti, Dipak Pariyar, Harikala Gharti, Deviram Gharti and Kuber BK were damaged, according to Deputy Superintendent of Police Rameshwor Twati of the District Police Office.

The buildings were rendered uninhabitable, forcing the affected families to move into neighbours’ homes and a nearby school, he said.

In Kaski, flooding on Friday damaged roads at several locations, disrupting transport.

The Modi river flood cut through the Birethanti-Ghandruk road at two locations in Annapurna Rural Municipality-8, severing road access to Ghandruk.

The rural road leading through Tikhedhunga to Ulleri, Ghorepani and Poon Hill was also cut off.

The flood also swept away two suspension bridges connecting Haijung in Annapurna Rural Municipality-6 with Deupur Mohoriya in Modi Rural Municipality-1 of neighbouring Parbat.

According to the Kaski District Police Office, the Modi river also eroded sections of the paved road along the riverbank at Birethanti. The river also damaged the road linking Chimrung and Syaulibazar to Sardikhola.

The erosion has put Birethanti, the gateway to popular tourist destinations including Ghandruk, Annapurna Base Camp and Ghorepani-Poon Hill, at risk.

The road from these areas to Pokhara runs through Birethanti and Nayapul before joining the Pokhara-Baglung section of the Mid-Hill Highway. With the road cut off at Birethanti, vehicles travelling towards the area have been stranded.

Assistant Chief District Officer Chitrangad Baral said the erosion had severed road access to all of wards 8, 9, 10 and 11 of Annapurna Rural Municipality. Electricity supplies were also disrupted after power poles were washed away at several locations.

Dozens of vehicles were stranded between Birethanti and Ghandruk, Baral said.

As of Friday, 45 four-wheelers, including passenger and private jeeps, buses, tractors, trucks and hydropower project tipper trucks, were stranded in the area. More than 25 motorcycles belonging to domestic tourists and residents were also unable to leave.

Eight foreign tourists and some domestic visitors were rescued and sent towards Pokhara, Baral said.

“There is no way to bring the tourists’ vehicles back to Birethanti, and there is no alternative route,” he said. “Once the water level in the Modi river drops, it could take up to one and a half months to repair the road and restore full access.”

The flood has also damaged the under-construction Upper Madi hydropower project in Hugu of Annapurna Rural Municipality-1.

Nepal Police spokesperson Abhi Narayan Kafle said police had identified vulnerable areas and safe locations in each district as part of the monsoon disaster preparedness and response plan.

“Rescue equipment has been serviced and kept ready according to the type of disaster it is meant to respond to,” he said. “Two platoons of specialised rescue personnel are on round-the-clock standby at the Nepal Police Disaster Response and Training Centre, while one platoon each is stationed at provincial police disaster management units for immediate mobilisation.”

A total of 10,085 police personnel have been deployed for disaster response, including at local police posts, Kafle said.

The Nepali Army has also stepped up preparations for the monsoon. It says it has trained 47,000 people at the central, provincial and district levels in disaster response.

Army spokesperson Rajaram Basnet said army units stationed in districts have kept designated personnel on standby with equipment needed for immediate rescue operations.

Search and rescue teams have been deployed at formations in all seven provinces, while a central-level team equipped with medical personnel is ready to conduct an air rescue within 15 minutes, he said.

“Specialised, trained personnel have also been kept on standby at the Nepali Army’s disaster management battalions in Sundarijal, Kathmandu, and Chitwan,” Basnet said. “A Nepali Army helicopter is also on round-the-clock standby in Surkhet.”

Boats and rafts have been prepared in areas prone to flooding, he added.

Thirteen buried as Thabang village struggles to recover

Sanju Pun Magar, 28, of Kotalbara in Thabang Rural Municipality-5, managed to save five members of her family when a landslide swept through the village on Wednesday evening.

When the ground suddenly began to shake, she grabbed her two-and-a-half-year-old son and rushed outside with her elderly grandmother, mother-in-law, sister-in-law and brother-in-law.

“It was raining heavily. There was thunder in the sky. Then we heard a sound like lightning striking and an earthquake hitting, and we panicked,” Sanju recalled. “When I stepped outside, the scene was terrifying. Then the electricity went out, and everything went dark. Even so, I got everyone out of the house, soaked from the rain.”

She was focused on getting her own family to safety. By then, however, the landslide had already buried a neighbour’s house and family.

She was focused on getting her own family to safety. By then, however, the landslide had already buried a neighbour’s house and family.

The roar of mud and floodwater was so loud that she could not hear people speaking or screaming, she said. Only after the rain eased did she realise that her neighbours’ house had been buried.

“There was no question of sleeping that night. We later learned that 13 people had been buried, apart from two who were injured. We only understood what had happened the next day,” she said. “The landslide has left the whole village looking like a pile of ruins.”

Sanju’s husband works for Nepal Police in Gulmi. Her sister-in-law lives in Sulichaur, where she runs a business, while her father-in-law has gone to Mustang in search of work.

“I came here from Upper Uwa after getting married eight years ago. I had never experienced anything as terrifying as Wednesday night,” Sanju said.

Her family stopped living in the house from Thursday because it is considered highly vulnerable to further landslides. She said finding a safe place for her 84-year-old grandmother, 65-year-old father-in-law and 50-year-old mother-in-law has become difficult because the family has nowhere else to live.

At around 7:30pm on Wednesday, a mudslide came down from the upper part of Sajang village in Uwa, above Kotalbara, burying 13 people and 12 houses, both large and small.

The bodies of only 10 of the victims have been recovered. Three people remain missing.

Resident Dhukaman Roka Magar said villagers are now struggling to find safe shelter for families whose homes remain standing but are still at risk.

“The whole village has been plunged into grief since Wednesday’s disaster. Three people are still missing, and we don’t know where to put the families who remain at risk,” he said.

Buddhi Gharti Magar, acting ward chairman of Thabang-5, where the landslide occurred, said officials were occupied with rescue efforts on Thursday and only began compiling details of affected families on Friday.

“Thirteen people from the village were buried at the same time. Only 26 people from the entire village are now left,” he said.

The Uwa river, where the landslide occurred, flows through Lungrī and joins the Madi river at Khungri before merging with the Airawati river in Pyuthan. By the time the Madi and Airawati rivers reach Bhalubang in Dang, they form the Rapti river.

articles.title: Nepse struggles to gain momentum as investors lose Rs7 billion in wealth
articles.summary:
The Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index fell 6.26 points, or 0.24 percent, over the trading week from August 10 to 14, closing at 2,643.83 points as investors remained cautious amid weak market confidence.

Trading activity also weakened. Total turnover stood at Rs18.40 billion, down 14.22 percent from Rs21.45 billion in the previous week. Average daily turnover over the five trading sessions was Rs3.68 billion.

Total market capitalisation fell to Rs4.547 trillion from Rs4.554 trillion a week earlier, wiping out around Rs7 billion in market value.

Nine of the 13 sectoral indices ended the week lower, while four gained.

The Trading sub-index recorded the steepest decline, falling 4.37 percent, or 148.04 points, to 3,239.86 points. The Finance index dropped 0.96 percent to 2,374.89, while the Manufacturing and Processing index fell 0.49 percent to 10,342.91.

The Hotel and Tourism sub-index was the top performer, rising 0.68 percent, or 49.52 points, to 7,338.95. The Microfinance index gained 0.30 percent to 4,576.54, while the Investment and Others indices each rose 0.24 percent.

The Sensitive Index, which tracks Class A companies, gained 1.17 points, or 0.25 percent, to 464.73. The Float Index fell 0.02 percent to 181.76.

Among individual stocks, Mount Everest Power Development recorded the biggest gain, rising 52.07 percent to Rs456.20. Sarvottam Paints climbed 32.23 percent to Rs396.70, while Ghalemdi Hydro and Khanikhola Hydropower gained 9.21 percent and 9.07 percent, respectively.

Mahila Lagubitta was the biggest loser, falling 21.05 percent to Rs1,279. Aatmanirbhar Lagubitta dropped 11.32 percent to Rs5,320, while Upper Lohore Khola Hydropower declined 9.76 percent to Rs342.

Energy companies dominated trading activity. Solu Hydropower recorded the highest turnover at Rs1.397 billion, although its share price fell 2.47 percent to Rs671. Ridi Power followed with Rs928.2 million, while NRN Infrastructure and Development recorded Rs688.7 million.

Ridi Power was also the most actively traded stock by volume, with 2.445 million shares changing hands. Its share price closed at Rs367.90.

Market analyst and former banker Jagannath Dhungel said he saw little indication of a sustained market recovery, with traders increasingly looking for opportunities to exit rather than hold shares for the long term.

“Investors are looking for a way out because confidence in the market has declined,” Dhungel said.

He attributed the weak sentiment to several factors, including the economic slowdown following the Covid-19 pandemic, uncertainty surrounding the new government, and ongoing investigations into market-related activities.

Growing supply without corresponding measures to increase demand is another concern, he said.

“Even though most companies have published comparatively improved financial statements, the market is slowing because traders are mostly looking for short-term gains,” Dhungel said.

He expects the market could see a short-term rise as mutual funds, which he said had sold shares towards the end of the previous fiscal year to maintain their financial reports, are likely to return to the market.

Investor and market analyst Subas Chandra Dhungana said the market has historically gained momentum in July and August, supported by the budget, monetary policy, and dividend season.

“This year, however, the market has not risen as expected because investors lack confidence,” he said.

Despite companies reporting better financial results at the end of the fiscal year, the market has struggled to gain momentum because Nepal’s stock market is largely driven by retail investors seeking short-term returns rather than dividends, Dhungana said.

The market also lacks enough institutional investors to absorb the growing supply of shares, he said.

For the market to regain short-term momentum, daily turnover would need to rise to around Rs8 billion to Rs9 billion, according to Dhungana. Current daily turnover is around Rs4 billion.

“Historically, the market tends to gain momentum around November,” he said.

articles.title: Nepal, India set three-year deadline to map cross-border land occupation
articles.summary:
In a major breakthrough, senior survey officials from Nepal and India have agreed to conclude the mapping of cross border occupation, a long-standing boundary issue between the two countries, within three years.

The 13th meeting of the Survey Officials' Committee (SOC), which concluded in Lucknow, India on Friday, agreed to determine the exact status of land occupation across the boundary with technological assistance.

“We have decided to use unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) to conclude mapping of cross border occupation in three years,” Susheel Dangol, deputy director at Department of Survey, told the Post over the phone from Lucknow. Dangol was leading the talks from the Nepal side.

The issue of cross-border occupation came into the spotlight after Prime Minister Balendra Shah told parliament in late May that, after assuming office, he learned that “not only has India encroached on Nepal’s land, but Nepal has also encroached on India’s land in multiple places.”

Later, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that Shah’s reference to Nepal having encroached on Indian land referred to the cross-border occupation and use of land, rather than to any territorial claim.

When the Nepal-India border was delineated, the Fixed Boundary Principle was adopted in riverine areas, resulting in situations of “cross-border occupation”, where citizens of one country cultivate and reside on land falling within the territory of the other country.

Over the decades, changes in the courses of hundreds of rivers have shifted thousands of hectares of land from one side of the border to the other. The SOC and the Joint Field Survey Teams are currently documenting these changes, and their findings will provide the technical basis for future decisions by the two governments, according to the officials.

When the 182 sets of strip maps were signed between Nepal and India in 2007, it was identified that nationals from both countries had either cultivated or resided on hundreds of hectares of land belonging to citizens of the other country.

“The UAVs will capture aerial images for the survey. We will then analyse those images and reach a common understanding to determine the extent of cross-border occupation,” said Dangol. He said the three-day meeting also approved the annual plan and budget for implementing the agreement.

Both the sides will start the joint survey soon after the monsoon season ends, around September or October.

The SOC is a subordinate committee of the Boundary Working Group (BWG), which is led by the heads of the survey departments of the two countries.

In its 2025 meeting, the BWG agreed to complete technical boundary work—including the joint construction of new boundary pillars and repair of damaged ones—within three years, except in the Susta and Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh areas.

Bilateral efforts to resolve technical boundary issues date back further, particularly to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s state visit to Nepal in 2014.

During the visit, the two sides agreed to establish the BWG, giving it a mandate to clear no-man’s land, construct, restore, and repair boundary pillars, update records of cross-border property holdings, and undertake other technical tasks related to border management.

According to the Department of Survey, 8,554 boundary pillars have been installed along the Nepal-India border. Of these, 1,325 are missing, while 1,956 are either partially or completely damaged. Under the BWG framework, the SOC and Joint Field Survey Teams provide technical expertise and carry out field-level work.

In 2015, the two sides set a three-year deadline to complete the technical work. After missing that target, they renewed the deadline in 2017, aiming to finish the work by 2022. That deadline also lapsed due to a combination of factors, including funding constraints, the Covid pandemic, recurring boundary disputes and adverse climatic conditions. Nepal and India share a 1,880-kilometre border spanning 27 districts.

articles.title: चुनदेवीको नेमप्लेट विवादको जिम्मा अदालतको हो : उपसभापति शर्मा
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले चुनदेवीको नेमप्लेटसँग सम्बन्धित विषयमा आफूले थप केही भन्न आवश्यक नरहेको बताएका छन्।

दोस्रो झापा-१ काठमाडौं कप फुटसल प्रतियोगिताका क्रममा सञ्चारमाध्यमसँग कुरा गर्दै शर्माले विशेष महाधिवेशनबाट आएको विषय भएकाले यसको निरूपण सम्बन्धित कानुनी प्रक्रियाबाटै हुने बताएका हुन्।

चुनदेवीको नेमप्लेटको विषयमा प्रश्न गर्दा उनले उक्त विषयको जिम्मेवारी अदालतकै रहेको स्पष्ट पारे। अदालतमा विचाराधीन विषयमा आफूले थप टिप्पणी गर्न नचाहेको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘यस विषयमा केही भन्नु छैन, सबै जिम्मा अदालतको हो,’ शर्माले भने।

शर्माले कांग्रेसभित्र पनि विधि र प्रक्रिया महत्वपूर्ण रहेको बताए। उनले खेलमा विधि र नियम भएजस्तै राजनीतिक दलभित्र पनि विधि र प्रक्रिया हुने भन्दै त्यसको पालना गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखेका छन्।

निवर्तमान सभापति शेरबहादुर देउवालाई सभापति भनेर सम्बोधन गर्दै नेमप्लेट राखेपछि विवाद बढेको हो। कांग्रेस नेता कान्छाराम तामाङले कसैलाई नसोधी देउवाको नेमप्लेट राखेको बताएका छन्।

चीनले जापानको बढ्दो सैन्य गतिविधिलाई लिएर कडा चेतावनी दिएको छ। चिनियाँ रक्षा मन्त्रालयका प्रवक्ता चेन सीले जापानले आफ्नो सैन्य विस्तार गरिरहेको र यसले क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षामा ठुलो खतरा निम्त्याउने बताएका हुन्।

जापानको रक्षा मन्त्रालयले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२७ का लागि झन्डै ५६ अर्ब डलरको बजेट प्रस्ताव गर्ने तयारी गरिरहेको बेला उनले यस्तो चेतावनी दिएका हुन्। यो रकम अहिलेसम्मकै उच्च हो। यही विषयलाई लिएर चेनले आफ्नो प्रतिक्रिया दिएको चिनियाँ सञ्चार माध्यमले जानकारी दिएका छन्।

articles.title: अमेरिकाद्वारा नेपालसहित १२ देशको टीपीएस खारेज : सात हजार नेपाली संकटमा, चार देशको मात्रै बाँकी
articles.summary:
अमेरिकामा डोनाल्ड ट्रम्प नेतृत्वको सरकारले नेपालसहित १३ वटा देशका नागरिकहरूलाई प्रदान गरिँदै आएको अस्थायी सुरक्षित स्थिति (टीपीएस) कार्यक्रम अन्त्य गर्ने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाएको छ।

अमेरिकी सर्वोच्च अदालतको जुन २०२६ को फैसला र विभिन्न संघीय अदालतहरूको आदेशसँगै सरकारले यो ठूलो अध्यागमन कटौतीलाई कानुनी रूपमा कार्यान्वयनमा ल्याएको हो। यससँगै अमेरिकाभर मानवीय सहायताका आधारमा वैधानिकता पाएका १० लाखभन्दा बढी विदेशी नागरिकहरूको कानुनी संरक्षण समाप्त वा संकटमा परेको छ। यस ऐतिहासिक निर्णयले गर्दा वर्षौंदेखि अमेरिकामा बसोबास गर्दै आएका आप्रवासी समुदायमा अचानक ठूलो चिन्ता, अन्योल र देश निकालाको गम्भीर संकट निम्तिएको छ।

यो नीतिगत परिवर्तनको सिधा असर अमेरिकामा रहेका करिब सात हजार २०० नेपाली नागरिकहरूमा परेको छ, जो अहिले गम्भीर कानुनी अनिश्चितताको भुँवरीमा परेका छन्। सन् २०१५ को विनाशकारी महाभूकम्पपछि अमेरिकी सरकारले नेपालीहरूका लागि पहिलो पटक यो मानवीय सुविधा उपलब्ध गराएको थियो। त्यसको सहयोगमा १२ हजारभन्दा धेरै नेपालीहरूले विगत एक दशकदेखि त्यहाँ व्यवसाय, रोजगारी र परिवार स्थापित गरेका थिए।

यद्यपि, विगत एक दशकमा साढे पाँच हजारभन्दा बढी नेपालीहरूले आफ्नो कानुनी हैसियत परिवर्तन गरी स्थायी बसोबास अनुमति (ग्रीन कार्ड) लिन सफल भइसकेका छन्। तर बाँकी रहेका करिब ७ हजार नेपालीहरूका लागि भने अब अमेरिकामा वैध रूपमा बस्ने र काम गर्ने यो विशेष ढोका बन्द भएको छ। अमेरिकी गृह सुरक्षा विभाग (डीएचएस) ले टीपीएस खारेज भएकाहरूलाई तत्कालै अन्य वैकल्पिक कानुनी बाटो खोज्न वा स्वदेश फर्कन निर्देशन दिएको छ।

ट्रम्प प्रशासनले आफ्नो कडा आप्रवासन नीतिअन्तर्गत नेपालसहितका देशहरू अब साविकको जस्तो संकटमा नरहेको र पुनरुत्थानको दिशामा गइसकेको तर्क गर्दै टीपीएस हटाएको हो। नेपालबाहेक यो कडा निर्णयको मारमा पर्ने अन्य देशहरूमा भेनेजुएला (सबैभन्दा धेरै करिब ६ लाख १६ हजार प्रभावित), हाइटी, सिरिया, यमन, अफगानिस्तान, क्यामरुन, होन्डुरस, निकारागुआ, दक्षिण सुडान, म्यानमार (बर्मा), सोमालिया र इथियोपिया रहेका छन्। हाल १२ देशको टीपीएस पूर्ण रूपमा खारेज भइसकेको छ भने इथियोपियाको खारेजी मात्र अदालती मुद्दाका कारण अस्थायी रूपमा रोकिएको छ।

सन् २०२६ को जुन महिनामा सर्वोच्च अदालतबाट मुलिन विरुद्ध डो मुद्दामा आएको फैसलाले आप्रवासी अधिकारवादी संस्थाहरूले दायर गरेका कानूनी चुनौतीहरूलाई निष्प्रभावी बनाइदिएपछि सरकारलाई विभिन्न देशको टीपीएस हटाउने बाटो खुला भएको हो। अदालतले टीपीएस खारेज गर्ने मन्त्रालयको निर्णय न्यायिक पुनरावलोकनको दायराभन्दा बाहिर रहने फैसला गरेपछि आप्रवासीहरूको कानूनी रक्षाकवच भत्किएको हो।

यस व्यापक खारेजी अभियानका कारण अमेरिकी टीपीएस कार्यक्रम अब निकै साँघुरो बनेको छ। पछिल्लो जानकारी अनुसार हाल अदालती विवादभन्दा बाहिर नियमित म्याद बाँकी रहेका प्रमुख देशहरूमा एल साल्भाडोर (सेप्टेम्बर ९, २०२६ सम्म), युक्रेन र सुडान (दुवै अक्टोबर १९, २०२६ सम्म), तथा लेबनान (नोभेम्बर २७, २०२६ सम्म) रहेका छन्। यद्यपि, वर्तमान प्रशासनको कठोर आप्रवासन नीतिका कारण सन् २०२६ को अन्त्यतिर म्याद सकिन लागेका यी बाँकी देशहरूको सुविधा पनि थप नवीकरण हुने सम्भावना निकै न्यून रहेको विज्ञहरू दाबी गर्छन्।

यस विषम परिस्थितिमा नेपाली आप्रवासी अधिकारवादी संस्थाहरूले प्रभावित नेपाली समुदायलाई धैर्य राख्न र नआत्तिन अनुरोध गरेका छन्। उनीहरूले वैध रूपमा अमेरिकामै टिकिरहनका लागि उपलब्ध कानुनी विकल्पहरूको खोजी गर्न तत्काल कदम चाल्न अपिल गरेका छन्। कानुनी विज्ञहरूका अनुसार योग्यता पुग्ने टीपीएस धारक नेपालीहरूले विद्यार्थी भिसा, रोजगारीमा आधारित भिसा वा अमेरिकी नागरिक रहेका परिवारका सदस्यहरूमार्फत आफ्नो कानुनी हैसियत परिवर्तन गर्ने प्रक्रिया तुरुन्तै सुरु गर्नुपर्छ।

नेपाली कांग्रेसका उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले चुनदेवीको नेमप्लेटसँग सम्बन्धित विषयमा आफूले थप केही भन्न आवश्यक नरहेको बताएका छन्।

चुनदेवीको नेमप्लेटको विषयमा प्रश्न गर्दा उनले उक्त विषयको जिम्मेवारी अदालतकै रहेको स्पष्ट पारे। अदालतमा विचाराधीन विषयमा आफूले थप टिप्पणी गर्न नचाहेको उनको भनाइ छ। ‘यस विषयमा केही भन्नु छैन, सबै जिम्मा अदालतको हो,’ शर्माले भने।

शर्माले कांग्रेसभित्र पनि विधि र प्रक्रिया महत्वपूर्ण रहेको बताए। उनले खेलमा विधि र नियम भएजस्तै राजनीतिक दलभित्र पनि विधि र प्रक्रिया हुने भन्दै त्यसको पालना गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखेका छन्।

निवर्तमान सभापति शेरबहादुर देउवालाई सभापति भनेर सम्बोधन गर्दै नेमप्लेट राखेपछि विवाद बढेको हो। कांग्रेस नेता कान्छाराम तामाङले कसैलाई नसोधी देउवाको नेमप्लेट राखेको बताएका छन्।

articles.title: मानुङकोट हाइकिङ जाँदा जङ्गलमा हराएका चार किशोरीको सकुशल उद्धार
articles.summary:
तनहुँको प्रसिद्ध पर्यटकीयस्थल मानुङकोट हाइकिङ जाने क्रममा जङ्गलमा बाटो बिराएर अलपत्र परेका चार जना किशोरीलाई प्रहरीले सकुशल उद्धार गरेको छ।

जिल्लाको व्यास नगरपालिका-५ ढोडेनीस्थित जङ्गलमा किशोरीहरू अलपत्र परेको सूचना प्राप्त हुनासाथ जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय तनहुँबाट प्रहरी टोली परिचालन गरिएको थियो।

प्रहरी सहायक निरीक्षक (प्रसनि) दीपा केसीको कमान्डमा महिला प्रहरीसहित खटिएको १० जनाको टोलीले शनिबार दिउँसो करिब १:१० बजे जङ्गलबाट उनीहरूको उद्धार गरेको हो।

उद्धार गरिएका चारै जना किशोरीलाई सकुशल परिवार तथा आफन्तको जिम्मा लगाइएको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: स्वास्थ्य बिमा अब पूर्णतः डिजिटल, घरबाटै सुविधा लिन सकिने
articles.summary:
स्वास्थ्य बिमा बोर्डले अनलाइनबाट बिमामा आबद्ध हुनसक्ने प्रक्रिया सुरु गरेको छ। बिमा कार्यक्रममा नयाँ आबद्धता, बिमालेख नवीकरण, सेवाग्राहीको व्यक्तिगत विवरण अद्यावधिक गर्ने (केवाइसी अपडेट) लगायत सबै काम अनलाइनामार्फत गर्न सकिने छ।

बोर्डका प्रवक्ता डा. पवनकुमार शाहले यसअघि बिमा कार्यक्रममा दर्ता सहयोगीमार्फत सर्वसाधरण बिमा आबद्ध हुने गरेकामा शुक्रबारदेखि सुरु गरिएको सेवामार्फत अनलाइनबाटै सबै विवरण र सेवा प्राप्त गर्न सकिने बताए।

‘हामीले बिमामा आबद्ध हुनका लागि अनलाइनामार्फत आफैँले फारम भर्न मिल्ने प्रणाली सुरु गरिसकेका छौं’, उनले भने, ‘अबदेखि दर्ता सहयोगीविना बिमा आबद्धता, नवीकरणलगायत सबै काम हुन्छन्।’

‘विद्युतीय माध्यमबाट स्वास्थ्य बिमामा आबद्धता तथा बिमालेख नवीकरणसम्बन्धी कार्यविधि, २०८३’ बमोजिम अनलाइनमार्फत बिमा आबद्धता र नवीकरण गर्न सुरु गरिएको प्रवक्ता शाहले बताए। उनका अनुसार यसका लागि ‘इसेवा’, ‘खल्ती’ र ‘कनेक्ट आइपिएस’ मार्फत भुक्तानी गर्न सकिने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ।

उक्त प्रणालीमार्फत व्यक्ति स्वयंले तथा दर्ता सहयोगीले परिवारलाई डिजिटल माध्यमबाट स्वास्थ्य बिमामा आबद्ध तथा बिमालेख नवीकरण गर्न सक्नेछन्।

अहिले बिमामा ५९ लाख ७० हजार ४०३ जना आबद्ध भएका प्रवक्ता शाहले बताए। उनको अनुसार स्वास्थ्य बिमा कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत पाँच जना परिवारसम्मका लागि तीन हजार ५०० बराबरको योगदानको आधारमा एक लाखसम्मको स्वास्थ्य सेवा उपलब्ध गराइन्छ

थप प्रतिसदस्य ७०० का दरले योगदान रकम थपिँदै जाने र प्रतिसदस्य २० हजार बराबरको सेवा सुविधा थपिने प्रावधान रहेको छ। यस्तै आठ प्रकारका कडा रोगमा एक लाख बराबरको थप सेवा प्रदान गरिने स्वास्थ्य बिमा बोर्डले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: मेचीनगरले जित्यो ‘झापा १-काठमाडौं कप फुटसल’ को उपाधि
articles.summary:
डिफेन्डिङ च्याम्पियन साविक मेचीनगरले दोस्रो झापा १-काठमाडौं कप फुटसल प्रतियोगिताको उपाधि जितेको छ।

फाइनल खेलमा शान्तिनगरलाई ३-० गोल अन्तरले स्तब्ध पार्दै मेचीनगरले लगातार दोस्रो पटक उपाधि रक्षा गरेको हो।

मेचीनगरको जितमा पात्थुङ्ग नेम्बाङ्ग, राजदीप अधिकारी र प्रतिक सुवेदीले समान एक-एक गोलको योगदान गरे।

यसअघि भएको प्रतिस्पर्धात्मक पहिलो सेमिफाइनलमा शान्तिनगरले ज्यामिरगढीलाई पेनाल्टी सुटआउटमा १०-९ गोल अन्तरले पराजित गर्दै फाइनल यात्रा तय गरेको थियो। अर्को सेमिफाइनलमा भने मेचीनगरले बाहुनडाँगीलाई २-० गोलले पन्छाएको थियो।

प्रतियोगितामा झापा क्षेत्र नम्बर-१ अन्तर्गतका साविक सात गाविस (मेचीनगर, दुवागडी, शान्तिनगर, चन्द्रगढी, ज्यामिरगढी, धाइजन र बाहुनडाँगी) को सहभागिता रहेको थियो।

प्रारम्भिक चरणको पहिलो खेलमा ज्यामिरगढीले चन्द्रगढीलाई ५-१ ले, दोस्रो खेलमा मेचीनगरले धाइजनलाई ७-० ले तथा तेस्रो खेलमा शान्तिनगरले दुवागडीलाई ७-३ गोल अन्तरले हराउँदै अन्तिम चारमा स्थान सुरक्षित गरेका थिए।

सात टोली मात्र सहभागी भएका कारण बाहुनडाँगीले भने सिधै ‘वाकओभर’ पाउँदै सेमिफाइनल खेलेको थियो।

प्रतियोगिताको विधागत पुरस्कारतर्फ च्याम्पियन टोली मेचीनगरका राजदीप अधिकारी सर्वोत्कृष्ट खेलाडी घोषित भए। यस्तै, मेचीनगरकै सोनिश श्रेष्ठ उत्कृष्ट गोलकिपर र सागर थापा उत्कृष्ट डिफेन्डर चुनिए।

शान्तिनगरका विमल तोलाङ्गी उत्कृष्ट स्ट्राइकर बन्दा ज्यामिरगढीका अनमोल राउत सर्वाधिक गोलकर्ता बने।

प्रतियोगिताअन्तर्गत कलाकार र राजनीतिकर्मीबीच मैत्रीपूर्ण फुटसल खेलसमेत आयोजना गरिएको थियो। जसमा कलाकारको टोलीले राजनीतिकर्मीको टोलीलाई ८-१ को फराकिलो गोल अन्तरले पराजित गर्‍यो।

कलाकारको जितमा मिलन खड्काले ह्याट्रिक गरे भने योगेन्द्र उपाध्याय र प्रशान्त शिवाकोटीले समान दुई-दुई गोल थपे।

मैत्रीपूर्ण खेलमा कलाकारको तर्फबाट चर्चित हास्य कलाकार मनोज गजुरेल, हेमन्त बुढाथोकी, कृष्ण शिवाकोटी, टिका भण्डारी, भानु ढकाललगायत मैदान उत्रिएका थिए।

यस्तै, राजनीतिकर्मीको टोलीबाट नेपाली कांग्रेसका उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्मा, नेकपाका रञ्जित तामाङ, नेकपा एमालेका एलपी साँवा र राप्रपाका भक्ति सिटौलालगायतले सहभागिता जनाएका थिए।

उपाधिसँगै विजेता मेचीनगरले नगद २१ हजार रुपैयाँ, ट्रफी र मेडल प्राप्त गर्‍यो भने उपविजेता बनेको शान्तिनगरले नगद ११ हजार रुपैयाँसहित ट्रफी र मेडल पायो।

काठमाडौं मेडिकल कलेजले स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी प्राविधिक सहयोग उपलब्ध गराएको उक्त प्रतियोगिताको उद्घाटन नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगन थापाले गरेका थिए भने विजयी खेलाडी तथा टोलीलाई नेपाली कांग्रेसका उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले पुरस्कार वितरण गरेका थिए।

articles.title: शशांक भन्छन्- कांग्रेस सभापतिका लागि म पनि इच्छुक नै छु
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका नेता डा. शशांक कोइरालाले पार्टीको आगामी १५ औं महाधिवेशनमा सभापति पदका लागि आफू पनि इच्छुक रहेको बताएका छन्।

यद्यपि, सभापतिमा उठ्ने विषयमा पार्टीका नेता-कार्यकर्तासँगको परामर्शपछि मात्र अन्तिम निर्णय लिने उनको भनाइ छ।

शनिबार सञ्चारकर्मीहरूसँग कुराकानी गर्दै नेता कोइरालाले नेतृत्वको दौडमा आफू पछि नहट्ने सङ्केत गरे। ‘पार्टी सभापतिको लागि म पनि इच्छुक त छु, तर मैले इच्छा गरेर मात्रै हुँदैन,’ उनले भने, ‘साथीहरूको केही भनाइ छ, त्यो पहिले सुन्नुपर्‍यो, अनि मात्र म निर्णय गर्छु।’

नेता डा. शेखर कोइरालाको उम्मेदवारीको सम्भावनाबारे सोधिएको प्रश्नमा उनले आफूहरूबीच राम्रो समझदारी रहेको सुनाए। ‘शेखरजी र मबीच धेरै राम्रो समझदारी छ, उहाँ सभापतिमा उठ्नुभयो भने पनि ठीकै छ, म सहयोग गरिहाल्छु,’ कोइरालाले भने।

सभापतिमा दाबेदारी प्रस्तुत गरे पनि पार्टी एकता जोगाउन आफू प्रतिबद्ध रहेको उनले दोहोर्‍याए। नेता कोइरालाले पार्टी विभाजन वा नयाँ दल गठनको चर्चालाई भने खारेज गरे। उनले भने, ‘म पार्टी फुटाउने वा नयाँ पार्टी खोल्ने पक्षमा विल्कुलै छैन। समस्या परे छलफल गरेरै एउटा निर्णयमा पुग्छौं।’

नेता कोइरालाले मुलुकमा सैद्धान्तिक विवाद समाप्त भइसकेकाले अब बन्ने कांग्रेस विकास, संगठन र युवा केन्द्रित नयाँ दिशामा अघि बढ्नुपर्ने बताए।

articles.title: Indian Army chief Seth arriving Sunday amid uncertainty over meeting with PM Shah
articles.summary:
Indian Army chief General Dhiraj Seth is arriving in Kathmandu on Sunday to receive the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army, although it is unclear whether he will meet Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

Nepal and India share a unique tradition under which the chief of the army of one country is accorded the honorary rank of general in the other. Indian Army chiefs visiting Nepal to receive the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army from the President have traditionally paid a courtesy call on the serving prime minister.

However, it remains unclear whether the tradition will continue this time, even hours before he arrives in Kathmandu. The Nepali Army leadership has already informed the Indian side that Shah and Seth will meet. “It is still not confirmed if General Seth will call on the prime minister,” an aide to Shah told the Post. “If there is a change in the plan, it will be communicated accordingly.”

The Indian side, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, had sought a meeting between the prime minister and General Seth, which was later sent to the Ministry of Defence and Nepali Army headquarters to manage the time.

Prime Minister Shah has maintained strict diplomatic protocol when meeting foreign diplomats and officials.

After four months in office, the prime minister only last week met separately with the Indian and Chinese ambassadors.

General Seth is visiting Nepal at the invitation of Chief of the Army Staff General Ashok Sigdel to receive the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army. Under the longstanding tradition between the two armies, President Ramchandra Paudel will confer the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army on Seth on Monday. Seth will also attend other events organised by the Nepali Army.

“Whenever a new army chief assumes office in either country, there is a tradition of exchanging high-level visits during which both chiefs are conferred with the honorary rank of General,” said Brigadier General Rajaram Basnet, spokesperson for the Nepali Army.

“I can confirm that General Seth is arriving in Kathmandu on Sunday and is going to receive the honorary rank of general from the President on Monday,” said Basnet. “The rest of his itinerary is dealt with by the Indian side.”

General Seth will be the first senior Indian official to visit Nepal since the formation of the Balendra Shah government on March 27. Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri had earlier been scheduled to visit Kathmandu, but the trip was postponed due to protocol-related reasons.

Sigdel was conferred with the honorary rank of General of the Indian Army by Indian President Droupadi Murmu in December 2024.

Some Indian media outlets suggested that during the visit, General Seth might raise the issue of stalled Agnipath recruitment in his meeting with Nepali officials. Recently, some former ex-Indian Gurkhas and youths staged rallies in Kaski and Lamjung districts demanding the resumption of Agnipath recruitment for Nepali youths.

In 2022, the Indian government revised the recruitment process in its army and announced the Agnipath scheme, under which personnel below officer ranks—soldiers, airmen and sailors who are not commissioned officers—are recruited for a period of four years. Nepal has not allowed its youths to be recruited into the Indian Army under the scheme. Under the scheme, only 25 percent of those recruited can continue in service, while the remaining 75 percent retire and receive a one-time gratuity.

articles.title: Hundreds of homes in eastern Rolpa at risk from landslides
articles.summary:
Hundreds of homes in eastern Rolpa face the threat of displacement after heavy rain triggered landslides and opened cracks across hillsides and beneath settlements.

The settlements at risk include Seram, Ghusbang and Gam in Sunchhahari Rural Municipality, and Uwa in Thabang Rural Municipality. A team led by the chief district officer has concluded that some of the settlements may have to be relocated.

Heavy rain throughout Thursday night heightened the landslide risk across much of eastern Rolpa. Homes in Seram and Ghusbang in Sunchhahari-1 are considered particularly vulnerable.

Dhani Man Roka, chairman of the ward, said cracks had appeared across the hills above the settlements.

“After raining throughout the night, the hillside above the village has split apart. Mud and debris have flowed down towards the settlement, while the ground below the village has also been torn open by landslides. It is no longer safe to stay there,” he said.

Roka said he and his family had moved to a safer open area near the forest after mud and debris flowed towards their home. He said he had advised other residents to take shelter in cattle sheds, forests and caves.

“We used a loudspeaker on Friday to tell residents not to stay in their homes because we fear more rain tonight. We have warned everyone to find a safe place to spend the night,” he said.

Seram has more than 100 households. Dalit families live mainly in the upper part of the village, while the lower section is predominantly inhabited by Magar families. Mud and debris have been coming down from Baima cliff and Gathan hill above the settlement.

Large cracks can be seen on the Baima cliff, from which mud has been flowing into the village, reaching the yards of some houses.

Two women were killed several weeks ago when a landslide came down from Gathan hill while they were out herding cattle.

“The village is below a cliff, and the soil is unstable. The ground breaks apart, and the soil turns into mud that flows down to the settlement. This time, much more debris came down, making the situation particularly dangerous,” Roka said.

The settlement has more than 100 households as well as the ward office, a school and a police post.

Ghusbang, also in Sunchhahari-1, has also suffered landslide damage. Floodwaters swept away a suspension bridge leading to a local micro-hydropower plant, while several houses have been damaged, according to Roka.

A full assessment has yet to be made because communication with the village has been disrupted.

Ghusbang lies east of Kotalbara in Uwa, where a landslide struck three days ago. Roka said police had been sent to Ghusbang after receiving reports that several houses and a community building had been destroyed.

More than 100 households live in Ghusbang. The village has no electricity supply, and residents said persistent rain has made it impossible even to rely on solar power for lighting.

Gam, in wards 2 and 3 of Sunchhahari Rural Municipality, is also at high risk of landslides. Four people were killed there after Thursday night’s rain triggered landslides that buried two houses in separate incidents.

In Thabang Rural Municipality-5, the large settlement of Uwa is also facing a serious landslide threat.

Buddhi Gharti Magar, chairman of the ward, said days of continuous rain had opened cracks across the village. According to him, all settlements in former Uwa Village Development Committee wards 1, 2, 4, 6 and 9 are at risk.

Residents said almost every household was affected by Thursday night’s rain.

Sita Pun said the risk of landslides had made it impossible for residents to remain in their homes.

All houses in former wards 2 and 6 are considered at high risk. Former ward 1 is also vulnerable, while homes in former wards 4 and 9 have suffered less damage.

More than 300 households live in Uwa’s main settlement. Resident Dhukman Roka said the village had been considered vulnerable for years.

Residents seek shelter in schools and cattle sheds

Authorities have advised residents living in high-risk areas to spend the night at a secondary school in Uwa, ward chairman Gharti Magar said.

“We have told people not to stay in homes at risk and to take shelter at the school or in cattle sheds considered safe. We issued the warning because more rain tonight could further increase the danger,” he said.

Those unable to fit into the school or cattle sheds have been advised to move to safer higher ground.

Gharti Magar said the settlements at risk would eventually have to be relocated.

Chief District Officer Ganga Bahadur Chhetri, who returned from an inspection of the Uwa landslide that killed 13 people, said authorities had concluded that vulnerable settlements in Uwa, Seram and Gam should be moved to safer locations.

“While conducting the field inspection, I contacted the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority from the site and briefed them on the situation and the problems faced by the residents,” Chhetri said. “The district disaster management committee is preparing to make a formal decision and send a written recommendation to the authority.”

A 60-member rescue team comprising personnel from the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force had travelled to Uwa under Chhetri’s leadership to inspect the damage and assist with rescue efforts.

The team became stranded on the road while returning on Thursday night.

“While returning after inspecting the Uwa incident and carrying out rescue work, we reached the stretch between Phuliban in Sunchhahari and Sirkyang cliff when heavy rain began. A landslide had blocked the road on the other side. We could not cross it, so we had to spend the entire night on the road. We were able to get out only in the morning,” Chhetri said.

articles.title: आज किन आएन हिजो चर्को स्वरमा उठाइएका प्रश्नको जवाफ ?
articles.summary:
नेकपा (एमाले) का महासचिव शङ्कर पोखरेलले विगतमा सडकका खाल्डा, सार्वजनिक सेवामा लामो लाइन, मलको अभाव र विदेशिने युवाको लर्कोलगायतका समस्या देखाउँदै नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको माग गरिए पनि अहिले सत्तामा पुगेकाहरूले न्यूनतम कार्यक्षमतासमेत देखाउन नसकेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्।

शनिबार सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्दै पोखरेलले हिजो चर्को स्वरमा उठाइएका प्रश्नको जवाफ आजको अवस्थाले खोजिरहेको बताएका हुन्।

उनले विगतमा देखाइएका दैनिक समस्या अझै समाधान हुन नसकेको र नागरिकमा भविष्यप्रतिको आशासमेत कमजोर हुँदै गएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

‘हिजो जुन समस्या देखाएर नेतृत्व बदल्न खोजिएको थियो, ती दैनिक समस्या अहिले पनि समाधान भएका छैनन् । भविष्यप्रतिको आशा जोगिन सकेको छैन र भूराजनीतिक असन्तुलन तथा असुरक्षा, साम्प्रदायिक एवं धार्मिक सद्भावमा खलबली तथा चरम निराशा र मानसिक तनाव बढिरहेका छन्,’ पोखरेलले लेखेका छन्।

पोखरेलले विगतमा उठाइएका प्रश्न स्मरण गर्दै अहिलेको अवस्थामाथि प्रश्न गरेका छन्। सडकका खाल्डा पुर्न नसक्नेले ठूला सपना बाँड्ने, सार्वजनिक सेवा लिन घण्टौँ लाइन बस्नुपर्ने, समयमा मल नपाइने र विमानस्थलमा विदेशिने युवाको लर्को लागिरहेको अवस्थामा विकासका गफ दिने भन्दै हिजो प्रश्न उठाइएको उनले बताएका छन्।

तर, आज ती दैनिक समस्या समाधान नभएको र नागरिकको भविष्यप्रतिको आशा पनि जोगाउन नसकिएको उनको टिप्पणी छ।

उनले मुलुकमा भूराजनीतिक असन्तुलन र असुरक्षा बढ्दै गएको, साम्प्रदायिक तथा धार्मिक सद्भाव खलबलिँदै गएको तथा चरम निराशा र मानसिक तनाव बढिरहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन्।

पोखरेलले हिजो यिनै समस्या देखाएर नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको हुटहुटी देखाइएको भए पनि सत्तामा पुगेपछि न्यूनतम कार्यक्षमता किन प्रदर्शन हुन सकेन भन्ने प्रश्नसमेत गरेका छन्।

‘अब अरूलाई दोष थोपरेर उम्किने छुट कसैलाई छैन,’ उनले लेखेका छन्।

सुधारका लागि चार सुझाव

देशको सुधारका लागि पोखरेलले चारवटा विषयमा जोड दिएका छन्। पहिलो, देश आर्थिक रूपमा सबल नभएसम्म आधारभूत समस्या पूर्ण रूपमा समाधान हुन नसक्ने यथार्थ स्वीकार गर्दै इमानदार पहलकदमी लिनुपर्ने उनको सुझाव छ।

त्यस्तै, दैनिक समस्याको गाँठो फुकाउँदै विकास र समृद्धिका दीर्घकालीन योजना पनि सँगसँगै अघि बढाउनुपर्ने उनले बताएका छन्।

संकटको समयमा एक्लै हिँड्ने हठ त्यागेर सहमति र सहकार्यको राजनीतिमा फर्किनुपर्ने तथा प्रशासनिक र सुरक्षा निकायलाई विश्वासमा लिएर संविधान र कानुनको पालना एवं सुधारमा जोड दिनुपर्ने पोखरेलको धारणा छ।

उनका अनुसार यी विषयलाई व्यवहारमा उतार्न सके सडकबाट सरकार बदल्नुपर्ने अवस्था दोहोरिन नदिने आधार तयार हुन सक्छ।

‘यति गर्न सके सडकबाट सरकार बदल्नुपर्ने नियति दोहोरिने छैन,’ पोखरेलले लेखेका छन्।

articles.title: एन्टिबायोटिक जथाभावी प्रयोग नगर्न सुझाव
articles.summary:
मधेस प्रदेशका मुख्यमन्त्री कृष्णप्रसाद यादवले एन्टिबायोटिक औषधिको जथाभावी प्रयोगले स्वास्थ्यमा गम्भीर जोखिम निम्त्याउन सक्ने भएकाले यसको प्रयोगमा सबै सचेत हुनुपर्ने बताएका छन् ।

जथाभावी एन्टिबायोटिक प्रयोगविरुद्ध जनकपुरधाममा आज आयोजित कार्यक्रममा मुख्यमन्त्री यादवले चिकित्सकको सल्लाहबिना एन्टिबायोटिक सेवन गर्ने, आवश्यकताभन्दा बढी प्रयोग गर्ने तथा चिकित्सकले तोकेको अवधिभन्दाअगावै औषधि सेवन गर्न छाड्ने प्रवृत्तिले भविष्यमा औषधिले काम नगर्ने अवस्था सिर्जना हुनसक्ने बताए ।

‘एन्टिबायोटिक औषधिको जथाभावी प्रयोगले स्वास्थ्य जोखिम बढ्न सक्छ, त्यसैले सबैले सचेत हुनु जरुरी छ’, उनले भने, ‘एन्टिबायोटिकको जथाभावी प्रयोगले स्वास्थ्य जोखिम बढ्नसक्छ भने कुरा सर्वसाधारणमा ज्ञान छैन, त्यसैले यसबारे जनचेतना जगाउनु आवश्यक छ ।’

स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी कुनै समस्या देखिएमा स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको परामर्श लिन, आफूखुसी औषधि प्रयोग नगर्न तथा चिकित्सकले तोकेको मात्रा र अवधिअनुसार मात्रै एन्टिबायोटिक सेवन गर्न उनले सबैसँग आग्रह गरे ।

एन्टिबायोटिकको प्रभावकारिता कायम राख्न सरकार, स्वास्थ्यकर्मी, औषधि व्यवसायी तथा सर्वसाधारण सबैको भूमिका महत्त्वपूर्ण हुने बताउँदै मुख्यमन्त्री यादवले औषधिको सही प्रयोगबारे जनचेतना अभिवृद्धि गर्न प्रदेश सरकारले आवश्यक पहल गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे ।

अभियानमा सहभागी चिकित्सकले भाइरल सङ्क्रमणमा एन्टिबायोटिक प्रभावकारी नहुने भएकाले सामान्य रुघाखोकीलगायत स्वास्थ्य समस्या देखिनेबित्तिकै आफूखुसी एन्टिबायोटिक सेवन गर्नु उपयुक्त नहुने सुझाव दिएका छन् । रासस

articles.title: सरकारको ताल यस्तै रहे मुलुकमा मध्यावधि चुनाव हुन्छ: शशांक
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका नेता डा. शशांक कोइरालाले वर्तमान सरकारको कार्यशैलीप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाउँदै सरकारले ठोस र जनपक्षीय काम गर्न नसकेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। उनले सरकारको काम गर्ने शैलीमा सुधार नआए मुलुक मध्यावधि निर्वाचनतर्फ जान सक्ने बताएका छन्।

शनिबार काठमाडौंमा नेपाली कांग्रेसको संस्थापन इतर पक्षले आयोजना गरेको राष्ट्रिय भेलाका क्रममा सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै कोइरालाले बहुमतको समर्थन प्राप्त सरकार भए पनि अहिलेसम्म कुनै नयाँ नीति तथा कार्यक्रम ल्याउन नसकेको बताए।

उनले वर्तमान सरकारलाई प्रभावकारी काम गर्न नसकेको भन्दै एक प्रकारको ‘कामचलाउ सरकार’को संज्ञा दिए। बहुमत भए पनि सरकारले जनताले अनुभूति गर्ने गरी ठोस काम गर्न नसकेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

“यो सरकार साधारण प्रकृतिको मात्र देखिएको छ। बहुमत भए पनि ठोस रूपमा कुनै राम्रो काम भएको मलाई लाग्दैन। नयाँ नीतिहरू केही छैनन्, यसलाई एक प्रकारको कामचलाउ सरकार नै भन्न सकिन्छ,” कोइरालाले भने।

उनले वर्तमान सरकार पाँच वर्षको पूर्ण कार्यकाल टिक्नेमा समेत आशंका व्यक्त गरे। राजनीतिक परिस्थितिमा परिवर्तन आउन सक्ने भन्दै उनले सरकारको कार्यशैली यस्तै रहे मुलुक मध्यावधि निर्वाचनमा जानुपर्ने अवस्था आउन सक्ने बताए।

“यो सरकार पाँच वर्ष नै टिक्छ भन्ने सुनिश्चितता छैन, बीचैमा मध्यावधि निर्वाचनमा जानुपर्ने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। राजनीतिमा यस्तो सम्भावनालाई नकार्न सकिँदैन,” उनले भने।

कोइरालाको यो अभिव्यक्तिले वर्तमान सरकारको कार्यसम्पादनप्रति कांग्रेसभित्रको असन्तुष्टि र आगामी राजनीतिक परिस्थितिबारे बढ्दो आशंकालाई समेत संकेत गरेको छ।

articles.title: मतदाताका समस्या सुन्दै गृहमन्त्री
articles.summary:
गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङ नागरिकका समस्या र गुनासा बुझ्न यतिबेला गृहजिल्ला गोरखामा छन् । आफ्नो निर्वाचन क्षेत्र गोरखा–१ का नागरिकका घरदैलोमा पुगी उहाँले स्थानीयस्तरमा भइरहेका विकास गतिविधि, सार्वजनिक सेवा प्रवाहलगायत विषयमा छलफल गरे ।

शुक्रबार गोरखा पुगेका गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले विकास आयोजनाको अनुगमनसहित जिल्लाको सुरक्षा अवस्थाबारे जानकारी लिएको प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी तुलसीबहादुर श्रेष्ठले बताए । ‘गृहमन्त्रीको कुनै औपचारिक कार्यक्रम छैन, निर्वाचन क्षेत्र भ्रमणका सिलसिलामा आउनुभएको हो’, उनले भने, ‘नागरिकसँग प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाट र संवाद गरिरहनुभएको छ ।’

शनिबार भीमसेन थापा गाउँपालिकाका स्थानीयवासीले सुकुमवासी व्यवस्थापन, नदी डुबानको समस्यालगायत विषय उठाएका थिए । गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले स्थानीयवासीका समस्या र गुनासा समाधानका लागि पहल लिने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएका थिए ।

सडक पूर्वाधार, खानेपानी, विद्युत्, सुरक्षा, रासायनिक मल अभाव, विपद् व्यवस्थापन, सार्वजनिक सेवा प्रवाहलगायत विषयमा गृहमन्त्री गुरुङ र स्थानीयवासीबीच छलफल भएको थियो ।

भेटघाटका क्रममा उनले नागरिकले भोग्दै आएका समस्या पहिचान गरी सम्बन्धित निकार्यमार्फत यथाशक्य छिटो समाधान गर्न सरकार प्रतिबद्ध रहेको बताए ।

गृहमन्त्री गुरुङले शान्ति सुव्यवस्था कायम गर्दै राज्यका सेवासुविधा छिटो, छरितो र पारदर्शी ढङ्गले नागरिकसम्म पुर्‍याइने बताए । गृहमन्त्री गुरुङ आइतबारसम्म आफ्नो निर्वाचन क्षेत्रमा रहने जनाइएको छ ।

articles.title: आज किन आएन हिजो चर्को स्वरमा उठाइएका प्रश्नको जवाफ ?
articles.summary:
नेकपा (एमाले) का महासचिव शङ्कर पोखरेलले विगतमा सडकका खाल्डा, सार्वजनिक सेवामा लामो लाइन, मलको अभाव र विदेशिने युवाको लर्कोलगायतका समस्या देखाउँदै नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको माग गरिए पनि अहिले सत्तामा पुगेकाहरूले न्यूनतम कार्यक्षमतासमेत देखाउन नसकेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्।

शनिबार सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्दै पोखरेलले हिजो चर्को स्वरमा उठाइएका प्रश्नको जवाफ आजको अवस्थाले खोजिरहेको बताएका हुन्।

उनले विगतमा देखाइएका दैनिक समस्या अझै समाधान हुन नसकेको र नागरिकमा भविष्यप्रतिको आशासमेत कमजोर हुँदै गएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

‘हिजो जुन समस्या देखाएर नेतृत्व बदल्न खोजिएको थियो, ती दैनिक समस्या अहिले पनि समाधान भएका छैनन् । भविष्यप्रतिको आशा जोगिन सकेको छैन र भूराजनीतिक असन्तुलन तथा असुरक्षा, साम्प्रदायिक एवं धार्मिक सद्भावमा खलबली तथा चरम निराशा र मानसिक तनाव बढिरहेका छन्,’ पोखरेलले लेखेका छन्।

पोखरेलले विगतमा उठाइएका प्रश्न स्मरण गर्दै अहिलेको अवस्थामाथि प्रश्न गरेका छन्। सडकका खाल्डा पुर्न नसक्नेले ठूला सपना बाँड्ने, सार्वजनिक सेवा लिन घण्टौँ लाइन बस्नुपर्ने, समयमा मल नपाइने र विमानस्थलमा विदेशिने युवाको लर्को लागिरहेको अवस्थामा विकासका गफ दिने भन्दै हिजो प्रश्न उठाइएको उनले बताएका छन्।

तर, आज ती दैनिक समस्या समाधान नभएको र नागरिकको भविष्यप्रतिको आशा पनि जोगाउन नसकिएको उनको टिप्पणी छ।

उनले मुलुकमा भूराजनीतिक असन्तुलन र असुरक्षा बढ्दै गएको, साम्प्रदायिक तथा धार्मिक सद्भाव खलबलिँदै गएको तथा चरम निराशा र मानसिक तनाव बढिरहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन्।

पोखरेलले हिजो यिनै समस्या देखाएर नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको हुटहुटी देखाइएको भए पनि सत्तामा पुगेपछि न्यूनतम कार्यक्षमता किन प्रदर्शन हुन सकेन भन्ने प्रश्नसमेत गरेका छन्।

‘अब अरूलाई दोष थोपरेर उम्किने छुट कसैलाई छैन,’ उनले लेखेका छन्।

सुधारका लागि चार सुझाव

देशको सुधारका लागि पोखरेलले चारवटा विषयमा जोड दिएका छन्। पहिलो, देश आर्थिक रूपमा सबल नभएसम्म आधारभूत समस्या पूर्ण रूपमा समाधान हुन नसक्ने यथार्थ स्वीकार गर्दै इमानदार पहलकदमी लिनुपर्ने उनको सुझाव छ।

त्यस्तै, दैनिक समस्याको गाँठो फुकाउँदै विकास र समृद्धिका दीर्घकालीन योजना पनि सँगसँगै अघि बढाउनुपर्ने उनले बताएका छन्।

संकटको समयमा एक्लै हिँड्ने हठ त्यागेर सहमति र सहकार्यको राजनीतिमा फर्किनुपर्ने तथा प्रशासनिक र सुरक्षा निकायलाई विश्वासमा लिएर संविधान र कानुनको पालना एवं सुधारमा जोड दिनुपर्ने पोखरेलको धारणा छ।

उनका अनुसार यी विषयलाई व्यवहारमा उतार्न सके सडकबाट सरकार बदल्नुपर्ने अवस्था दोहोरिन नदिने आधार तयार हुन सक्छ।

‘यति गर्न सके सडकबाट सरकार बदल्नुपर्ने नियति दोहोरिने छैन,’ पोखरेलले लेखेका छन्।
